text: When, however, our time was up, we left and started on our journey; and all of them, with wives and children, were escorting us on our way until we were out of the city; then, kneeling down on the beach, we prayed,

title: Acts 21:6
text: and said good-bye, and went on board the ship, while they returned home again.

title: Acts 21:7
text: And when we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we reached Ptolemais, and greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.

title: Acts 21:8
text: On the morrow we started for Caesarea, where we went into the house of Philip, the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.

title: Acts 21:9
text: Now Philip had four unmarried daughters who prophesied,

title: Acts 21:10
text: and while we remained there many days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

title: Acts 21:11
text: He came to us, and taking Paul's girdle, he bound his own feet and hands, saying, "Thus says the Holy Spirit, `so will the Jews at Jerusalem bind the owner of this girdle, and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.'"

title: Acts 21:12
text: As soon as we heard these words, both we and those who were standing near entreated Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

title: Acts 21:13
text: "What do you mean by thus breaking my heart with your grief?" answered Paul. "For I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem, for the name of the Lord Jesus."

title: Acts 21:14
text: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, "The will of the Lord be done."

title: Acts 21:15
text: A few days after this we took up our luggage and went up to Jerusalem.

title: Acts 21:16
text: And some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us. They led us to the house of Mnason, a Cypriote, a disciple of long standing, with whom we were to lodge.

title: Acts 21:17
text: At length we reached Jerusalem, and the brothers there received us gladly.

title: Acts 21:18
text: On the following day we went with Paul to call on James, and all the elders were present.

title: Acts 21:19
text: After saluting them Paul rehearsed, one by one, the things that God had done among the Gentiles by his ministry.

title: Acts 21:20
text: And they, when they heard it, glorified God, and said to him: "You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews, of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the Law.

title: Acts 21:21
text: "Now what they have been told about you, again and again, is that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles, to forsake Moses, and not to circumcise their children, nor to follow the old customs.

title: Acts 21:22
text: "What then ought to be done? They will certainly hear that you are come.

title: Acts 21:23
text: "So do this that we tell you.

title: Acts 21:24
text: "We have four men here under a vow; associate yourself with them, purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses so that they may have their heads shaved; then every one will know that there is no truth in the rumors that they have heard about you; but that you yourself walk orderly obeying the law.

title: Acts 21:25
text: "As for the Gentile believers, we wrote giving judgment that they should abstain from anything sacrificed to an idol, from blood, from what is strangled, and from fornication."

title: Acts 21:26
text: Then Paul took the men, and after purifying himself with them next day, went into the temple to declare the fulfilment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.

title: Acts 21:27
text: But when the seven days were almost over, the Asiatic Jews caught sight of him in the temple, and began to stir up all the crowd, and laid hands on him, shouting:

title: Acts 21:28
text: "Men of Israel, help! This is the man who goes everywhere preaching to everybody against the people, and the Law, and this place. And he has actually brought Gentiles even into the temple, and has desecrated the holy place."

title: Acts 21:29
text: (For they had formerly seen Trophimus, the Ephesian, with him in the city, and supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.)

title: Acts 21:30
text: The whole city was thrown into uproar. The mob surged together, seized Paul, and began to drag him outside the temple. Whereupon the doors were at once shut.

title: Acts 21:31
text: While they were attempting to kill him, news came to the tribune [commander of the garrison] that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

title: Acts 21:32
text: At once he took soldiers and centurions, and rushed down upon them. When they saw the tribune and the troops, they left off beating Paul.

title: Acts 21:33
text: Then the tribune came up and seized him, and ordered that he be bound with two chains. "Who is he?" he began asking, "and what has he done?"

title: Acts 21:34
text: Some among the crowd kept shouting one thing, some another; and when the tribune could not learn the facts because of the uproar, he ordered Paul into the barracks.

title: Acts 21:35
text: When was going up the steps, he had to be carried by the soldiers, because of the violence of the mob,

title: Acts 21:36
text: for the whole mass of the people were following him, shouting, "Away with him!"

title: Acts 21:37
text: Just as he was about to be taken into the barracks, Paul said to the tribune, "May I speak to you?"

title: Acts 21:38
text: "Do you know Greek?" said the tribune; "Are you not, then, the Egyptian who in days gone by stirred up to sedition, and let into the wilderness the four thousand cutthroats?"

title: Acts 21:39
text: "I am a Jew," answered Paul, "a native of Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city. And I pray you, give me permission to speak to the people."

title: Acts 21:40
text: So when he had given leave, Paul stood on the stairs, beckoning with his hands to the people. There came a great hush, and he spoke to them as follows, in Hebrew:

title: Acts 22:1
text: "Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make in your presence."

title: Acts 22:2
text: When they heard him speaking in Hebrew they became the more quiet.

title: Acts 22:3
text: "I am a Jew," he said, "born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, taught according to the strict manner of the Law of our forefathers, ardent for God, even as you all are this day.

title: Acts 22:4
text: "I persecuted to the death this way, continually binding and delivering up to prisons both men and women.

title: Acts 22:5
text: "To this the high priest and all the council of elders are witnesses. It was from them that I received letters to the brothers in Damascus, and I was already on my way to bring those also who were there back to Jerusalem, in bonds, for punishment.

title: Acts 22:6
text: "But when, on my journey, I was nearing Damascus, about noon, suddenly a great light from heaven shone round about me.

title: Acts 22:7
text: "I fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to me, "`Saul! Saul! why are you persecuting me?'

title: Acts 22:8
text: "`Who are you, Lord?' I asked. "`I am Jesus, the Nazarene, whom you are persecuting,' he answered me.

title: Acts 22:9
text: "Now my companions, though they beheld the light, did not hear the words of Him who spoke to me.

title: Acts 22:10
text: "And I said, `What shall I do, Lord?' and the Lord said to me, `Rise and go into Damascus, and there you will be told about all that you are destined to do.'

title: Acts 22:11
text: "And as I was seeing nothing for the glory of the light, I was led by the hand of my companions, and so came into Damascus.

title: Acts 22:12
text: "And a certain Ananias, a pious man according to the Law, well thought of by all the Jews who lived there,

title: Acts 22:13
text: "came to me, and standing by me, said to me, "`Brother Saul, receive your sight' "In that very hour I regained my sight and looked up at him.

title: Acts 22:14
text: "Then he said: "`The God of our forefathers has appointed you to know his will; and to see the righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.

title: Acts 22:15
text: "`For before the face of all men you will be a witness for him of what you have seen and heard.

title: Acts 22:16
text: "`And now why do you wait? Rise and be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling upon his name.'

title: Acts 22:17
text: "After my return to Jerusalem, and while I was praying in the temple,

title: Acts 22:18
text: "I fell into a trance and saw him saying to me, "`Make haste and go quickly out of Jerusalem, because they will not receive your testimony concerning me.'

title: Acts 22:19
text: "`Lord,' I replied, `they themselves well know that I was beating and imprisoning in synagogue after synagogue those who believed in you,

title: Acts 22:20
text: "`and when the blood of your martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by and consenting, and holding the garments of his murders.'

title: Acts 22:21
text: "`Depart,' he said to me, `for I will send you forth, far hence, to the Gentiles.'"

title: Acts 22:22
text: Until they heard this last statement, the people were listening to Paul, but now they roared out: "Away with such a fellow from the earth! He is not fit to live!"

title: Acts 22:23
text: When they continued to shout, throwing their clothes into the air, and flinging dust around,

title: Acts 22:24
text: the tribune ordered him to be brought into the barracks, and examined under the lash, to learn for what reason the people were thus crying out against him.

title: Acts 22:25
text: But when they had tied him up with the thongs, Paul said to the centurion who was standing near, "If a man is a Roman citizen, and uncondemned, is it lawful for you to scourge him?"

title: Acts 22:26
text: When the centurion heard that, he went to the tribune and said to him: "What are you intending to do? This man is a Roman citizen."

title: Acts 22:27
text: So the tribune came to Paul and asked him, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?" "Yes," he said.

title: Acts 22:28
text: "I paid a large sum to get this citizenship," said the tribune. "But I was citizen-born," said Paul.

title: Acts 22:29
text: Then those who were about to scourge him, immediately left him. And the tribune too, was afraid, when he learned that Paul was a Roman citizen, for he had had him bound.

title: Acts 22:30
text: The next day, as he wished to learn the real reason why the Jews accused Paul, he unbound him, and commanded the chief priests and all the Sanhedrin to come together, and brought Paul down, and placed him before them.

title: Acts 23:1
text: With a stedfast gaze at the Sanhedrin, Paul said, "Brothers, I have lived with a good conscience before God to this day."

title: Acts 23:2
text: Then the High Priest Ananias ordered those who stood near Paul to strike him on the mouth.

title: Acts 23:3
text: "You whited sepulcher," exclaimed Paul, "God will strike you! You are sitting there to judge me according to the law, are you? And do you command me to be struck, contrary to the Law?"

title: Acts 23:4
text: "Do you rail at God's high priest?" said the bystanders.

title: Acts 23:5
text: "Brothers, I did not know that he was the high priest," exclaimed Paul, "for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of a ruler of my people."

title: Acts 23:6
text: Then perceiving that half the Sanhedrin were Sadducees and the other half Pharisee, he cried out in the Sanhedrin: "Brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of Pharisees! It is for the hope of the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial!"

title: Acts 23:7
text: When he said this, there arose a quarrel between the Pharisees and Sadducees; the meeting was divided.

title: Acts 23:8
text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel nor spirit; the Pharisees affirm them all.

title: Acts 23:9
text: Then a great clamor arose; some of the scribes who belonged to the Pharisaic party stood up, and contended: "We find nothing wrong in this man. What if a spirit has spoken to him, or an angel?"

title: Acts 23:10
text: But when the dissension became violent, the tribune, fearing that they would tear Paul in pieces, ordered the troops to march down and take him by force from among them, and bring him into the barracks.

title: Acts 23:11
text: And the following night the Lord stood by him and said: "Be of good courage; for as you have borne faithful witness concerning me at Jerusalem, so you must testify at Rome also."

title: Acts 23:12
text: When day dawned the Jews made a conspiracy, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

title: Acts 23:13
text: And there were more than forty who had sworn this oath.

title: Acts 23:14
text: They went to the high priests and elders, and said to them: "We have bound ourselves by a solemn oath to eat nothing until we have killed Paul.

title: Acts 23:15
text: "Now do you and the Sanhedrin ask the tribune to bring him down to you, as though you would judge his case more exactly; and we are ready to kill him, before he comes near the place."

title: Acts 23:16
text: But Paul's sister's son heard of their intended attack, and he went and got into the barracks, and told Paul.

title: Acts 23:17
text: And Paul called one of the centurions, and said, "Take this young man to the tribune, for he has something to tell him."

title: Acts 23:18
text: So he took him, and brought his to the tribune, and said, "Paul, the prisoner, called me to him, and begged me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you."

title: Acts 23:19
text: And the tribune took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, "What is it that you have to tell me?"

title: Acts 23:20
text: "The Jews," he answered, "have agreed to ask you to bring down Paul tomorrow to the Sanhedrin, as though they wish to examine his case in detail.

title: Acts 23:21
text: "Now do not let them persuade, for more than forty men are lying in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse, not to eat nor drink until they have killed him; even now they are all ready, awaiting your consent."

title: Acts 23:22
text: So the tribune sent the young man home with the injunction, "Tell no man that you have given me this information."

title: Acts 23:23
text: Then he called two centurions to him and said: "Get ready by nine o'clock tonight two hundred infantry to march as far as Caesarea, and also seventy troopers and two hundred spearmen."

title: Acts 23:24
text: He further ordered them to provide horses on which to mount Paul, so as to bring him safely to Felix, the governor.

title: Acts 23:25
text: He also wrote a letter in the following terms:

title: Acts 23:26
text: "Claudius Lysais unto the Most Excellent Governor Felix, greeting.

title: Acts 23:27
text: "This man Paul had been seized by the Jews, and was about to be killed by them, when I came upon them with the troops, and rescued him, as I had learned that he was a Roman citizen.

title: Acts 23:28
text: "Anxious to find out why they had accused him, I brought him down to their Sanhedrin.

title: Acts 23:29
text: "Here I learned that he was accused about questions of their law, but was not charged with anything worthy of death or imprisonment.

title: Acts 23:30
text: "Now when I received information that there would be a plot against the man, I sent him at once to you, charging his accusers also to speak against him before you."

title: Acts 23:31
text: So the soldiers took Paul, as they were bid, and brought him by night to Antipatris.

title: Acts 23:32
text: Next day the infantry returned to the barracks, leaving the troopers to ride on with him.

title: Acts 23:33
text: They reached Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, and also presented Paul before him.

title: Acts 23:34
text: After reading the letter, he asked to what province he belonged, and when he understood that he was of Cilicia, he said,

title: Acts 23:35
text: "I will hear your case when your accusers also are come." And he ordered him to be kept in custody in Herod's palace.

title: Acts 24:1
text: Five days later, Ananias the high priest came down to Caesarea with some of the elders, and with an orator, named Tertullus. They laid information before the governor against Paul.

title: Acts 24:2
text: So Paul was sent for, and then Tertullus began to accuse him, saying: "As it is owing to your excellency that we enjoy profound peace, and that the state of this nation,

title: Acts 24:3
text: "owing to your wise care, has been improved in every respect and in every place, we accept it with profound thankfulness.

title: Acts 24:4
text: "But not to weary you too much, I beg of your Excellency to listen to a few words from us.

title: Acts 24:5
text: "For we have found this fellow a pest, an inciter of insurrection among all the Jews of the empire, and a ringleader in the heresy of the Nazarenes.

title: Acts 24:6
text: "He even tried to profane the Temple, but we arrested him.

title: Acts 24:7
text: "Then the chief captain, Lysias came and violently took him from us.

title: Acts 24:8
text: From him you will be able, by examining Paul yourself, to learn the truth of all these charges we are bringing against him."

title: Acts 24:9
text: The Jews also joined in the charge, maintaining that these were the facts.

title: Acts 24:10
text: Then at a nod from the governor, Paul spoke: "Because I know that for many years you have been a judge in this nation, I feel encouraged to make my defense.

title: Acts 24:11
text: "For you have it in your power to know that it is not more than twelve days ago that I went up to Jerusalem to worship;

title: Acts 24:12
text: "and that neither in the Temple, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city, did they find me disputing with any man or stirring up a crowd.

title: Acts 24:13
text: "Nor can they prove the charges which they are now bringing against me.

title: Acts 24:14
text: "But this I confess to you, that I worship the God of our ancestors, according to the Way which they call a heresy, believing everything that is according to the Law, or is written in the Prophets,

title: Acts 24:15
text: "and having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there is to be a resurrection both of the just and the unjust.

title: Acts 24:16
text: "Hence I too endeavor to have a conscience void of offense toward God and men alway.

title: Acts 24:17
text: "Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and to offer sacrifices.

title: Acts 24:18
text: "While I was thus engaged, they found me in the temple, purified, with no crowd and no uproar. But there were certain Asiatic Jews

title: Acts 24:19
text: "who ought to have been here before you, and to have made accusations if they had anything against me.

title: Acts 24:20
text: "Or let these men themselves say what fault they found, when I appeared before the Sanhedrin!

title: Acts 24:21
text: "Unless it was for this one sentence which I uttered when I stood and cried, `It is for the resurrection of the dead that I am on my trial today before you.'"

title: Acts 24:22
text: At this point Felix, who had a pretty accurate knowledge of the Way, adjourned the case, saying to the Jews, "When Lysias the tribune comes down, I will go carefully into the matter."

title: Acts 24:23
text: And he gave orders to the centurion that Paul should be kept in custody, but treated with indulgence, and that his personal friends were not to be forbidden to minister to him.

title: Acts 24:24
text: Some days later Felix came, with his wife Drusilla, a Jewess; he sent for Paul, and listened to him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.

title: Acts 24:25
text: And as he reasoned about morality, self-control, and the future judgment, Felix was terrified, and said, "For the present go on your way, and when I find a convenient season, I will send for you."

title: Acts 24:26
text: He was hoping that Paul would give him money, and for this reason he used to send for him often to converse with him.

title: Acts 24:27
text: But after two full years Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and because he wished to curry favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul still in prison.

title: Acts 25:1
text: Three days after Festus entered his province, he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

title: Acts 25:2
text: The high priest and the Jewish leaders laid charges against Paul before him.

title: Acts 25:3
text: They urged him, asking it as a favor, to send for him to Jerusalem. They meant to lay in wait for him and kill him on the way.

title: Acts 25:4
text: But Festus answered that Paul was in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was going there soon.

title: Acts 25:5
text: "Let those then," he said, "who are in authority among you, go down with me, and if there is anything amiss in the man, let them accuse him."

title: Acts 25:6
text: After staying not more than eight or ten days among them, he went down to Caesarea, and the next day, after taking his seat upon the tribunal, he ordered Paul to be brought.

title: Acts 25:7
text: When he came in, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him and brought a number of serious charges against him, which they could not prove.

title: Acts 25:8
text: Paul said in his defense, "I have committed no crime against the Law of the Jews, against the Temple, or against Caesar."

title: Acts 25:9
text: But Festus, wishing to ingratiate himself with the Jews, answered Paul and said, "Will you go up to Jerusalem and be tried there by me upon these charges?"

title: Acts 25:10
text: "I am standing before Caesar's tribunal," answered Paul, "where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you very well know.

title: Acts 25:11
text: "If I am a criminal and have done anything for which I ought to die, I do not object to die. But if none of their charges is true, no man can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar."

title: Acts 25:12
text: Then Festus, after conferring with the council, answered: "You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you shall go."

title: Acts 25:13
text: A short time after this King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.

title: Acts 25:14
text: And while they tarried many days, Festus laid Paul's case before the king. "There is a man here," he said, "whom Felix left a prisoner.

title: Acts 25:15
text: "The chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me about him, when I was at Jerusalem, demanding a sentence against him.

title: Acts 25:16
text: I told them that it was not the custom of the Romans to give any man up for punishment, before the accused had his accusers face to face, and had opportunity of defending himself against the charges that had been brought against him.

title: Acts 25:17
text: "So when a number of them came together here, I made no delay, but the next day took my seat in the tribunal, and commanded the man to be brought.

title: Acts 25:18
text: "But when his accusers stood up, they did not begin charging him with any of the crimes that I was expecting,

title: Acts 25:19
text: but they kept quarreling with him about certain matters connected with their own religion, and about one Jesus who had died, but whom Paul affirmed over and over was alive.

title: Acts 25:20
text: I was perplexed how to investigate such questions, and asked Paul whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.

title: Acts 25:21
text: But when Paul appealed to have his case reviewed for the decision of the Emperor, I ordered him to be detained until I could send him up to Caesar."

title: Acts 25:22
text: "I should like to hear the man, myself," said Agrippa to Festus. Festus answered, "You shall hear him tomorrow."

title: Acts 25:23
text: So the next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp, and took their places in the hall of audience, accompanied by the tribunes and men of high rank in the city. At the command of Festus Paul was brought in.

title: Acts 25:24
text: "King Agrippa," said Festus, "and all men who are present with us, you see here the man about whom the entire body of the Jews at Jerusalem, and here also, sent to me, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.

title: Acts 25:25
text: "I could not find that he had done anything for which he ought to die; but as he himself has appealed to the Emperor, I have determined to send him.

title: Acts 25:26
text: "Now I have nothing very definite to tell our sovereign about him. So I have brought the man before you all, and especially before you, King Agrippa, in order that, after examination, I may have something to write.

title: Acts 25:27
text: "For it does seem to me unreasonable to send a person without signifying the charges against him."

title: Acts 26:1
text: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "You are permitted to speak for yourself." So Paul stretched forth his hand and began to make his defense:

title: Acts 26:2
text: "I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you this day, in regard to all the accusations brought against me by the Jews;

title: Acts 26:3
text: "especially since you are an export in all Jewish customs and questions. I pray you, expert in all Jewish customs and questions. I pray you, hear me with patience.

title: Acts 26:4
text: "The kind of life I have lived from my youth upward among my own nation and at Jerusalem, all that early life of mine, is well known to all the Jews.

title: Acts 26:5
text: "They know me of old, if they are willing to testify, how that according to the strict sect of our religion, I lived a Pharisee.

title: Acts 26:6
text: "Today I am standing trial because of the hope of the promise made by God to our ancestors,

title: Acts 26:7
text: "a promise which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving God night and day, hope to attain. It is concerning this hope, King Agrippa, that I am accused by the Jews.

title: Acts 26:8
text: "Why is it deemed incredible by you all, if God raises the dead?

title: Acts 26:9
text: "I indeed once thought with myself that I ought to do many things against the name of Jesus, the Nazarene.

title: Acts 26:10
text: "And this also I did in Jerusalem. Armed with authority from the chief priests, I shut up many of the saints in prison, and when they were condemned to death I gave my vote against them.

title: Acts 26:11
text: "In all the synagogues also I punished them oftentimes, and tried to make them blaspheme; and in my mad fury I was pursuing them even to foreign cities.

title: Acts 26:12
text: "On this errand I was traveling to Damascus one day, armed with authority and commission of the chief priests,

title: Acts 26:13
text: "when at noon, as I journeyed, O King, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and around those who journeyed with me.

title: Acts 26:14
text: "We all fell to the ground; and I heard a voice saying to me in Hebrew: "`Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goad.'

title: Acts 26:15
text: "`Who are you, Lord?' I said. "And the Lord said: `I am Jesus whom you are persecuting.

title: Acts 26:16
text: "`But rise and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you in order to appoint you my minister and my witness both of what you have already seen and of those things in which I will appear to you.

title: Acts 26:17
text: "`I will deliver you from the Jewish people, and from the Gentiles to whom I am sending you to open their eyes

title: Acts 26:18
text: "`so that they may turn from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, in order to receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me.'

title: Acts 26:19
text: "So then, O King Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision;

title: Acts 26:20
text: "but I proceeded to preach, first to those in Damascus, and then in Jerusalem and throughout all the country of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they must repent and turn to God and do deeds worthy of repentance.

title: Acts 26:21
text: "For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple, and tried to kill me.

title: Acts 26:22
text: "But having obtained the help that comes from God, I stand even to this day witnessing both to small and great, saying nothing except what the prophets and Moses said should come;

title: Acts 26:23
text: "how that the Christ must suffer, and how he should be the first to rise from the dead, and should bring a message of light to the Jewish people and to the Gentiles."

title: Acts 26:24
text: As Paul thus made his defense, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice: "Paul, you are raving mad; your great learning is driving you mad."

title: Acts 26:25
text: "I am not mad, most noble Festus," said Paul,

title: Acts 26:26
text: "I am speaking words of sober truth. For the King, to whom I am speaking freely, knows of these matters. I am persuaded that not one of these things has escaped his notice; for these things were not done in a corner.

title: Acts 26:27
text: "King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe."

title: Acts 26:28
text: Agrippa answered, "In short, you are doing your best to persuade me to become a Christian."

title: Acts 26:29
text: "Long or short," answered Paul, "my prayer to God is that not only you but all who are my hearers this day might become such as I am, save for these chains."

title: Acts 26:30
text: Then the king rose, and Bernice, and those who were sitting with him.

title: Acts 26:31
text: When they had withdrawn they continued talking to one another. "This man is doing nothing," they said, "for which he deserves death or imprisonment."

title: Acts 26:32
text: And Agrippa said to Festus, "If he had not appealed to Caesar, he might have been set free."

title: Acts 27:1
text: When it was decided that we should sail for Italy, they proceeded to hand over Paul and a few other prisoners to the custody of Julius, a centurion of the Imperial Regiment.

title: Acts 27:2
text: We embarked in a ship of Adramyttium which was about to sail to the ports of the province of Asia, and put to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, accompanied us.

title: Acts 27:3
text: The next day we touched at Sidon. There Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him leave to visit his friends and refresh himself.

title: Acts 27:4
text: Putting to sea from thence we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were against us;

title: Acts 27:5
text: and after sailing across the Cilician and Pamphylian waters, we came to Myra, in Lycia.

title: Acts 27:6
text: And there the centurion found an Alexandrian ship bound for Italy, and put us on board of her.

title: Acts 27:7
text: For many days we sailed slowly, and then arrived with difficulty over against Cnidus; from this point, as the wind did not further favor us, we ran under the lee of Crete, off Cape Salmone;

title: Acts 27:8
text: and coasting along with difficulty we reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.

title: Acts 27:9
text: By this time the season was far advanced, and sailing had become dangerous (for the Autumn Fast was past); so Paul began to warn them:

title: Acts 27:10
text: "Sirs," he said to them, "I perceive that the voyage will be attended with injury and serious loss, not only to the cargo and to the ship, but also to our own lives."

title: Acts 27:11
text: But the centurion paid greater heed to the master and to the owner than to anything that was spoken by Paul;

title: Acts 27:12
text: and as the harbor was ill adapted for winter quarters, the majority advised putting out to sea from thence, to see whether they could get to Phoenix and winter there, a harbor on the coast of Crete facing northeast and southeast.

title: Acts 27:13
text: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close in shore.

title: Acts 27:14
text: But it was not long before a furious wind, called Euroclydon, rushed down from the island;

title: Acts 27:15
text: when the ship was caught and could not face the wind, we gave way to it, and let her drive.

title: Acts 27:16
text: Then we ran under the lee of a little island named Claudia, where with great difficulty we were able to secure the ship's boat.

title: Acts 27:17
text: After hauling it aboard, they used ropes to undergird the ship, and since they were fearful lest they should be driven upon the Syrtes, they lowered the gear and lay to.

title: Acts 27:18
text: And as we were being terribly battered by the storm, the next day they began to throw the freight overboard,

title: Acts 27:19
text: and on the third day with their own hands they threw the ship's tackling overboard.

title: Acts 27:20
text: Then when for many days neither sun nor stars were seen, and a great tempest still beat upon us, all hope that we should be saved was now taken away from us.

title: Acts 27:21
text: When for a long time they had been without food, Paul stood among them and said: "Men, you ought to have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete, and so have spared yourselves this injury and loss.

title: Acts 27:22
text: "But now take courage. There will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship,

title: Acts 27:23
text: "for last night an angel of the God whose I am and whom I serve, stood by me and said:

title: Acts 27:24
text: "`Fear not, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you the lives of all who are sailing with you.'

title: Acts 27:25
text: "So take courage, men! I believe God, I believe that things will turn out exactly as it has been told me.

title: Acts 27:26
text: "But we must be cast upon a certain island."

title: Acts 27:27
text: It was now the fourteenth night, and we were drifting through the Adriatic Sea when, about midnight, the sailors began to suspect that they were drawing near to some land.

title: Acts 27:28
text: So they sounded and found twenty fathoms; and after a little they sounded again, and found fifteen fathoms.

title: Acts 27:29
text: Then, fearing lest we should run ashore on the rocks, they threw out four anchors from the stern, and longed for day to come.

title: Acts 27:30
text: And when the sailors were trying to flee from the ship, and had lowered the boat into the sea under pretext of laying anchors from the bow,

title: Acts 27:31
text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, "Unless these men remain on the ship, you cannot be saved."

title: Acts 27:32
text: Then the soldiers cut the ropes of the ship's boat and let her fall off.

title: Acts 27:33
text: And while day was dawning, Paul kept urging them all to take some food: "This is the fourteenth day," he said, "that you have been on the watch, fasting, having eaten nothing.

title: Acts 27:34
text: "So I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety. For there shall not a hair perish from the head of any one of you."

title: Acts 27:35
text: When he had so said and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God before them all, and broke it and began to eat.

title: Acts 27:36
text: Then they all cheered up and themselves took food.

title: Acts 27:37
text: There were in the ship two hundred and seventy-six souls, all told.

title: Acts 27:38
text: After eating a hearty meal, they began to lighten the ship by throwing the wheat overboard.

title: Acts 27:39
text: When it was day they tried in vain to recognize the land, but they spied an inlet with a sandy beach, and they began conferring to see whether they could drive the ship into it.

title: Acts 27:40
text: They cast off the anchors and left them in the sea, and unloosing at the same time the ropes that tied the rudders, they hoisted the foresail to the breeze, and headed for the beach.

title: Acts 27:41
text: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; the bow struck and remained fixed, but the stern began to break up under the violence of the waves.

title: Acts 27:42
text: Now the soldiers were planning to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim off and so escape.

title: Acts 27:43
text: But the centurion kept them from their purpose, because he wished to save Paul. He gave orders that those who could swim should first jump overboard and get to land;

title: Acts 27:44
text: and that the rest should follow, some on planks and some on other bits of wreckage. And so it came to pass that all escaped safe to the land.

title: Acts 28:1
text: And when we were escaped, we ascertained that the island was called Malta.

title: Acts 28:2
text: The foreign-speaking people showed us uncommon kindness, for they lighted a fire and made us all welcome, because of the rain and because of the cold.

title: Acts 28:3
text: Now when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and thrown them on the fire, a viper crawled out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

title: Acts 28:4
text: When the natives saw the reptile hanging on his hand, they began saying to one another, "No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet justice does not allow him to live."

title: Acts 28:5
text: However, he shook off the reptile into the fire and received no harm.

title: Acts 28:6
text: But they kept expecting him to swell up or fall down dead suddenly. But after waiting a long time, and seeing no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said over and over that he was a god.

title: Acts 28:7
text: Now in the neighborhood there were estates belonging to the governor of the island, whose name was Publius. He received us and entertained us for three days courteously.

title: Acts 28:8
text: It happened however that the father of Publius was lying ill of fever and dysentery. So Paul went to see him and prayed and laid his hands on him and healed him.

title: Acts 28:9
text: After this all the other sick people on the island came, and continued to be restored to health.

title: Acts 28:10
text: These loaded us with many honors and, when at last we set sail, they put on board such things as we needed.

title: Acts 28:11
text: Three months passed before we set sail an Alexandrian ship which had wintered in the island. Its name was "The Twin Brothers."

title: Acts 28:12
text: And touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

title: Acts 28:13
text: From thence, tacking round, we reached Rhegium. Next day a south wind sprang up, which brought us in a day to Puteoli.

title: Acts 28:14
text: There we found brothers who invited us to stay a week with them. Then we reached Rome.

title: Acts 28:15
text: From there the brothers, when they heard about us, came out to meet us as far as the Appian Forum and the Three Taverns. When Paul saw them he thanked God and took courage.

title: Acts 28:16
text: When we finally entered Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself with the soldier to guard him.

title: Acts 28:17
text: Now three days later he called the leading Jews together, and when they were come together he said to them: "Brothers, I was delivered a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans, though I had done nothing against the people or the customs of your fathers.

title: Acts 28:18
text: "Then when they had examined me they wanted to set me at liberty because there was no cause of death in me.

title: Acts 28:19
text: "But when the Jews objected I was forced to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything to accuse my nation of.

title: Acts 28:20
text: This is the reason why I begged you to see and speak with me. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain."

title: Acts 28:21
text: They said to him: "We neither received any letters about you from Judea nor has any brother come hither to report or speak any harm of you.

title: Acts 28:22
text: "But we are eager to hear from you what it is that you believe; for we all know that as for this sect it is everywhere spoken against."

title: Acts 28:23
text: So they arranged a day with him and came to him in his lodgings in great numbers. He expounded the matter to them; testifying to the Kingdom of God, and persuading them about Jesus, from morning till evening, both from the Law of Moses and from the Prophets.

title: Acts 28:24
text: Some began to believe what he said, but some were unbelieving.

title: Acts 28:25
text: Unable to agree among themselves, they began to go, but not before Paul had spoken a word to them, saying: "Right well did the Holy Spirit say to your ancestors, through the prophet Isaiah:

title: Acts 28:26
text: "Go to the people and tell them, You will hear and hear, and by no means understand; And will look, and by no means see.

title: Acts 28:27
text: For this people's heart is grown obtuse, Their ears are heavy of hearing, Their eyes have they closed, Lest they should see with their eyes And hear with their ears, Lest they understand with their heart, And turn again, and heal them.

title: Acts 28:28
text: "Be fully assured, therefore, that this salvation of God is now sent unto the Gentiles. They will listen to it."

title: Acts 28:29
text: When he finished speaking, the Jews departed, and reasoned among themselves.

title: Acts 28:30
text: After this Paul lived for two whole years in his own rented house, and used to receive all who came to see him.

title: Acts 28:31
text: He continued to preach the kingdom of God, and to teach about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, quite unmolested.

title: Romans 1:1
text: From Paul, a slave of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for a gospel of God,

title: Romans 1:2
text: which through his prophets he promised beforetime, in holy writings;

title: Romans 1:3
text: this gospel is concerning his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, who was born of David's posterity in respect of his bodily nature,

title: Romans 1:4
text: but was by his resurrection from the dead instated as Son of God, with power, in respect of his spirit of holiness.

title: Romans 1:5
text: It is through him, even Jesus Christ our Lord, that I received grace and apostleship to promote obedience to the faith among all the Gentiles, for his name's sake;

title: Romans 1:6
text: among whom you also are called to be Jesus Christ's:

title: Romans 1:7
text: To all that are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: May God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ, bless you, and give you peace.

title: Romans 1:8
text: First I thank my God, through Jesus Christ, for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed throughout all the world.

title: Romans 1:9
text: God is my witness, to whom I render holy service in my spirit in the gospel of his Son, how unceasingly I am ever making mention of you in my prayers,

title: Romans 1:10
text: always entreating him that now at length, if such be his will, the way may be made clear for me to come to you.

title: Romans 1:11
text: For I am longing so to see you, in order to impart to you some spiritual gift, so that you may be established;

title: Romans 1:12
text: that is, that I with you may be encouraged by you, each of us by the other's faith, yours and mine.

title: Romans 1:13
text: I want you to know, brothers, that many a time I have planned to come to you--though until now I have been hindered--so as to have some harvest-fruit among you also, even as I have among the rest of the Gentiles.

title: Romans 1:14
text: To Greeks and to barbarians, to the cultured and to the uncultured, I have a debt to discharge.

title: Romans 1:15
text: So much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you also who are in Rome.

title: Romans 1:16
text: FOR I AM PROUD OF THE GOSPEL. IT IS GOD'S SAVING POWER FOR EVERY ONE WHO BELIEVES. FOR THE JEW FIRST, AND ALSO FOR THE GENTILE.

title: Romans 1:17
text: FOR IN IT IS BEING REVEALED A RIGHTEOUSNESS WHICH PROCEEDS FROM GOD, FROM FAITH UNTO FAITH; AS IT IS WRITTEN.

title: Romans 1:18
text: For God's wrath is ever being revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men who smother the truth by their unrighteousness.

title: Romans 1:19
text: This is so because that which may be known of God is manifest among them; for God has made it manifest to them.

title: Romans 1:20
text: For ever since the creation of the world his invisible nature, even his everlasting power and divinity, has been clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made. So they have no excuse.

title: Romans 1:21
text: For although they knew God, yet they did not glorify him as God, nor give him thanks; but became vain in their reasoning, and their senseless minds were darkened.

title: Romans 1:22
text: While they professed to be wise, they became fools,

title: Romans 1:23
text: and exchanged the majesty of the imperishable God for an idol, graven in the likeness of perishable man, or of birds and four-footed beasts and creeping things.

title: Romans 1:24
text: So God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to impurity, to the dishonoring of their own bodies;

title: Romans 1:25
text: because they exchanged the truth of God for an untruth, and worshiped and served the creature, rather than the Creator who is blessed forever. Amen.

title: Romans 1:26
text: That is why God has given them up to passions of dishonor; for on the one hand their women actually changed the natural function of sex into that which is against nature;

title: Romans 1:27
text: and on the other hand their men likewise abandoned the natural use of women, and were ablaze with passion for one another; men with men practising shameless acts and receiving in their own person that recompense of their wrong-doing which necessarily followed.

title: Romans 1:28
text: And just as they refused to continue to retain God in their knowledge, so did God cast them out to an outcast mind, to do those things which were indecent.

title: Romans 1:29
text: They were overflowing with every kind of iniquity, depravity, greed, and malice. They were full of envy, murder, quarreling, deceit, and malignity.

title: Romans 1:30
text: They became whisperers, back-biters, hated of God, insolent, haughty, boastful. They invented sins. They were disobedient to parents.

title: Romans 1:31
text: They were without sense, without faith, without natural affection, without mercy.

title: Romans 1:32
text: Though they knew well the ordinance of God, that those who practise such vices are worthy of death, they not only continue to do the same, but were even applauding those who practise vice.

title: Romans 2:1
text: You are therefore inexcusable, O man, whoever you are, that sits in judgment; for in judging another you are condemning yourself. You, the judge, are habitually practising the very same things.

title: Romans 2:2
text: "We know that God's judgment against those who practise such vices is in accord with the truth," you say?

title: Romans 2:3
text: Very well; and do you suppose, you who judge those that practise such vices, and are doing the very same, that you will elude the judgment of God?

title: Romans 2:4
text: Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and long patience? Do you not know that the kindness of God is leading you to repentance?

title: Romans 2:5
text: In your hardness and impenitence of heart you are treasuring up for yourself wrath on the Day of Wrath, when the righteous judgment of God is revealed.

title: Romans 2:6
text: For He will render to every man according to his works;

title: Romans 2:7
text: eternal life to those who by patience in well-doing strive for glory and honor and immortality;

title: Romans 2:8
text: but anger and wrath upon those who are self-willed and disobey the truth, but obey unrighteousness.

title: Romans 2:9
text: Anguish and calamity will be upon every soul of man who practises evil, upon the Jew first, and also upon the Gentile;

title: Romans 2:10
text: but glory and honor and peace to every man who does good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile.

title: Romans 2:11
text: For there is no partiality with God.

title: Romans 2:12
text: For all who have sinned without law will also perish without law; and all who have sinned under law will be judged by law.

title: Romans 2:13
text: For it is not the hearers of law who are righteous in the eyes of God; nay, it is the doers of law who will be accounted righteous.

title: Romans 2:14
text: For when Gentiles, who have no law, obey by natural instinct the commands of the Law, they even though they have no law, are a law to themselves.

title: Romans 2:15
text: For they show that the work of the Law is written in their hearts, while their conscience bears them witness, as their reasonings accuse, or it may be defend, them,

title: Romans 2:16
text: in the day when God will judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ, according to my gospel.

title: Romans 2:17
text: Now if you bear the name of a Jew, and rely upon law, and boast yourself in God,

title: Romans 2:18
text: and know his will, and can test the things that differ; if you are instructed out of the Law,

title: Romans 2:19
text: and are confident that you yourself are a darkness,

title: Romans 2:20
text: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of the young, because you have in the Law the form of knowledge and of the truth--well then, you who are teaching others, do you ever teach yourself?

title: Romans 2:21
text: You who are preaching that a man should not steal, do you practise theft?

title: Romans 2:22
text: You who keep saying that a man should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who hold idols in abhorrence, are you plundering their temples?

title: Romans 2:23
text: You who are making your boast in the Law, do you habitually dishonor God through your transgressions of the Law?

title: Romans 2:24
text: For the name of God is continually blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, even as the Scripture itself says.

title: Romans 2:25
text: Circumcision does indeed profit, if you are obedient to the Law; but if you habitually break the Law, your circumcision is become uncircumcision.

title: Romans 2:26
text: So if the uncircumcised keeps the ordinance of the Law, shall not his uncircumcision be reckoned equivalent to circumcision.

title: Romans 2:27
text: And shall not those who are physically uncircumcised, but who keep the Law, condemn you who are a breaker of the Law, although you have a written law and circumcision?

title: Romans 2:28
text: For the real Jew is not the man who is one outwardly, and the real circumcision is not outward in the flesh;

title: Romans 2:29
text: but the real Jew is one inwardly, and real circumcision is heart-circumcision, spiritual, not literal, praised not by men, but by God.

title: Romans 3:1
text: What special privilege, then, has the Jew? Or what is the use of circumcision?

title: Romans 3:2
text: Much in every way. First of all, because to them were entrusted the oracles of God.

title: Romans 3:3
text: Supposing some of them have proved faithless?

title: Romans 3:4
text: By no means! Be sure that God is ever true, though all mankind prove false. As it is written, That thou mayest be found just in thine argument, And gain thy cause when thou contendest.

title: Romans 3:5
text: But if our unrighteousness thus brings out God's righteousness, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous--I speak after the manner of men--when he inflicts his anger on us?

title: Romans 3:6
text: Be it far from us; for in that case how could God judge the world?

title: Romans 3:7
text: But if by a falsehood of mine the truthfulness of God has been made to redound to his glory, why am I still tried as a sinner?

title: Romans 3:8
text: And why not say (as I myself am slanderously reported to say), "Let us do evil that good may come out of it"? Such arguments are rightly condemned.

title: Romans 3:9
text: What then? Are we Jews in a better position? Not at all, for I have already charged all, both Jews and Gentiles, with being under sin.

title: Romans 3:10
text: As it is written: There is none righteous, no, not one;

title: Romans 3:11
text: There is none that understands, none that seeks for God!

title: Romans 3:12
text: All have swerved from the right path; Every one of them has become corrupt. There is none that practises good, no, not one.

title: Romans 3:13
text: Their throat is an open grave; With their tongues they have used deceit. The venom of asps is under their lips.

title: Romans 3:14
text: Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.

title: Romans 3:15
text: Their feet are swift to shed blood.

title: Romans 3:16
text: Destruction and ruin are in their paths;

title: Romans 3:17
text: And the path of peace they have not known.

title: Romans 3:18
text: Reverence for God is not before their eyes.

title: Romans 3:19
text: Now we know that whatever the Law says, it speaks to those who are under the Law; so that every mouth may be shut, and all the world may be brought under the judgment of God.

title: Romans 3:20
text: For no man will be justified in God's sight by works of the Law; for through the Law comes the consciousness of sin.

title: Romans 3:21
text: But now, quite apart from any law, a righteousness coming from God has been fully brought to light, continually witnessed to by the Law and the Prophets.

title: Romans 3:22
text: I mean a righteousness coming from God through faith in Jesus Christ, for all who believe. For there is no distinction between Jew and Gentile,

title: Romans 3:23
text: since all have sinned and lack the glory which comes from God;

title: Romans 3:24
text: but they are now being justified by his free grace through the deliverance that is in Christ Jesus.

title: Romans 3:25
text: For God openly set him forth for himself as an offering of atonement through faith, by means of his blood, in order to show forth his righteousness--since in his forbearance he had passed over the sins previously committed--to show forth his righteousness,

title: Romans 3:26
text: I say, at this present time; that he himself might be just, and yet the justifier of him who has faith in Jesus.

title: Romans 3:27
text: Then what becomes of boasting? It is shut out. What sort of law forbids it? A law of works? No, but a law of faith.

title: Romans 3:28
text: For I conclude that a man is justified by faith, altogether apart from the deeds of the Law.

title: Romans 3:29
text: Is God then the God of the Jews alone, and not of the Gentiles also? He is God of the Gentiles also,

title: Romans 3:30
text: since there is one God who will justify the circumcised through faith, and by their faith will he justify the uncircumcised.

title: Romans 3:31
text: Do we then render law invalid through faith? Certainly not; on the contrary we make it stand.

title: Romans 4:1
text: What then shall we say of Abraham, our ancestor in the flesh?

title: Romans 4:2
text: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to be proud of, but not before God.

title: Romans 4:3
text: For what does Scripture say? And Abraham believed God, and it was set down to his account as righteousness.

title: Romans 4:4
text: Now if a man earn his pay by his work, it is not counted to him as a favor, but it is paid him as a debt;

title: Romans 4:5
text: but a man who does not "work," but believes in him who justifies the ungodly, has his faith imputed to him for righteousness.

title: Romans 4:6
text: Just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the man to whom God imputes righteousness apart from actions.

title: Romans 4:7
text: Blessed [he says] are they whose iniquities have been forgiven, And whose sins have been covered.

title: Romans 4:8
text: Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.

title: Romans 4:9
text: Is this blessing, then, for the circumcised alone? or for the uncircumcised also? Abraham's faith, I say, was imputed to him for righteousness.

title: Romans 4:10
text: How then was it imputed to him? When he was circumcised? or uncircumcised? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision;

title: Romans 4:11
text: and he received circumcision as a sign, a seal of the faith-righteousness which he had while he was in uncircumcision; in order that he might be the father of all who believe, even though they are uncircumcised; so that righteousness might be imputed to them.

title: Romans 4:12
text: He is the father of circumcision to those who are not merely circumcised, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham which he held while he was as yet uncircumcised.

title: Romans 4:13
text: For the promise that he should be heir of the world did not come to Abraham or to his posterity through law, but through faith-righteousness.

title: Romans 4:14
text: For if those who are righteous through law are heirs, faith is empty and the promise becomes void.

title: Romans 4:15
text: For law works wrath; but where there is no law, neither is there transgression.

title: Romans 4:16
text: This is why righteousness is of faith, that it may be a free gift; so that the promise stands firm to all Abraham's posterity; not to his children of his faith. For in the sight of the God in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead, and calls into being that which is not, Abraham is the father of us all [both Jews and Gentiles],

title: Romans 4:17
text: as it is written, I have made you a father of many nations.

title: Romans 4:18
text: For Abraham, hoping against hope, had faith to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, So numberless shall your descendants be.

title: Romans 4:19
text: Though he was about a hundred years old, his faith did not fail him when he regarded his own body, now as good as dead. and remembered Sarah's barrenness.

title: Romans 4:20
text: Nor did he with regard to the promise of God waver in unbelief, but he waxed strong in faith, while he gave God glory,

title: Romans 4:21
text: and was fully persuaded that what God had promised, he was able also to perform.

title: Romans 4:22
text: And so his faith was reckoned to him for righteousness.

title: Romans 4:23
text: Now these words were not written simply for his sake, but for us as well.

title: Romans 4:24
text: For it will be "reckoned for righteousness." to us also, who believe on him that raised from the dead our Lord Jesus;

title: Romans 4:25
text: who was betrayed to death for our transgressions, and raised again to life for our justification.

title: Romans 5:1
text: Since we stand justified as the result of faith, let us continue to enjoy the peace we have with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.

title: Romans 5:2
text: Through him also we have had our access into this grace in which we have taken our stand, and are exulting in hope of the glory of God.

title: Romans 5:3
text: And not only so, but we are actually exulting also even in our troubles; for we know that trouble works fortitude,

title: Romans 5:4
text: and fortitude character, and character, hope--

title: Romans 5:5
text: a hope which never disappoints us. For through the Holy Spirit who has given to us, the "brimming river of the love of God" has overflowed in our hearts.

title: Romans 5:6
text: For while we were still without strength, Christ died in due time for the ungodly.

title: Romans 5:7
text: Why, a man will hardly give his life for another, even for a righteous man, though perchance for a good man one might even take it upon himself to die.

title: Romans 5:8
text: But God gives proof of his love to us by the fact that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

title: Romans 5:9
text: By how much more, then, being now justified in his blood, shall we be saved through him from the wrath of God.

title: Romans 5:10
text: For if, when we were God's enemies, we were reconciled to him through the death of his Son, how much more, now that we are reconciled, shall we be saved in his life.

title: Romans 5:11
text: And not only that, but we exult in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now obtained our reconciliation.

title: Romans 5:12
text: Thus, then, sin came into the world through one man, and through sin came death and so death spread to all men, because all had sinned.

title: Romans 5:13
text: For prior to the Law, sin actually existed in the world, but sin was not set down to man's account when there was no law.

title: Romans 5:14
text: Nevertheless, from Adam to Moses death reigned as king, even over those who had not sinned after the likeness of Adam's transgression. Now Adam is a type of Him who was to come.

title: Romans 5:15
text: But the free gift is not like the transgression; for if through the transgression of that one man the rest on men died, much more did the grace of God and the gift given in his grace in the one Man, Jesus Christ, overflow unto the rest of men.

title: Romans 5:16
text: And it is not with the free gift as it was through the one that sinned; for the judgment came from one transgression unto condemnation; but the free gift came from many transgressions unto acquittal.

title: Romans 5:17
text: For if through the transgression of the one, death reigned as king through the one, much more shall those who receive the overflowing grace and gift of righteousness reign as kings in life through One, through Jesus Christ.

title: Romans 5:18
text: It follows then, as through the transgression of one man came condemnation unto all men, even so through the act of righteousness of One came acquittal and life to all men.

title: Romans 5:19
text: For just as through the disobedience of one man the rest were made sinners; even so by the obedience of One shall all the rest be made righteous.

title: Romans 5:20
text: Now law was brought in so that transgression might abound; but where sin abounded, grace super-abounded;

title: Romans 5:21
text: in order that as sin has ruled as king in death, so also grace might rule as king in righteousness which issues in eternal life, through Jesus Christ our Lord,--ours!

title: Romans 6:1
text: What then shall we say? Shall we continue to abound in sin, in order that grace may come to abound?

title: Romans 6:2
text: No indeed; how shall we who have died to sin still go on living in it any longer?

title: Romans 6:3
text: For do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Jesus Christ, have been baptized into his death?

title: Romans 6:4
text: We have been buried together with him, then, through baptism into his death, in order that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so also we should live in a newness of life.

title: Romans 6:5
text: For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, so we shall also be united with him in the likeness of his resurrection.

title: Romans 6:6
text: For this we know, that our old self was crucified with Christ, in order that the slave of sin might be destroyed; so that we should no longer be in slavery to sin--

title: Romans 6:7
text: for he who is dead is set free from sin.

title: Romans 6:8
text: Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him;

title: Romans 6:9
text: knowing that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more; death has no more dominion over him.

title: Romans 6:10
text: For the death that he died, he died unto sin once for all; but the life that he lives he is living unto God.

title: Romans 6:11
text: Even so count yourselves also to be dead unto sin, but alive unto God in Christ Jesus.

title: Romans 6:12
text: Therefore let not sin rule as king in your mortal body, compelling you to obey its lusts.

title: Romans 6:13
text: Do not continue to present any part of your body to sin to be used as a weapon of unrighteousness. On the contrary, be presenting yourselves to God, as alive from the dead, and the various parts of your bodies to be used as weapons of righteousness.

title: Romans 6:14
text: For sin shall not lord it over you; for you are not under the rule of law, but under the rule of grace.

title: Romans 6:15
text: What then? Shall we commit an act of sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Certainly not.

title: Romans 6:16
text: Do you not know that when you surrender yourselves as slaves to any one to obey him, you are his slaves whom you obey; whether it be sin, whose end is death, or obedience, whose end is righteousness?

title: Romans 6:17
text: But God be thanked that you who were once the slaves of sin have obeyed from your hearts that type of teaching to which you were appointed;

title: Romans 6:18
text: and being set free from sin, you became the slaves of righteousness--

title: Romans 6:19
text: I speak in these homely figures because of the weakness of your fleshly nature--just as you once surrendered your faculties into slavery to impurity and to all lawlessness, so now you must surrender your faculties into slavery to righteousness, unto deeds of holiness.

title: Romans 6:20
text: For when you were the slaves of sin, you were under no subjection to righteousness.

title: Romans 6:21
text: What harvest-fruit then had you at that time in the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.

title: Romans 6:22
text: But now that you have been set free from sin and become slaves of God, the harvest-fruit which you are reaping tends to produce holiness, and it ends is life eternal.

title: Romans 6:23
text: FOR THE POOR WAGES OF SIN IS DEATH, BUT THE FREE GIFT OF GOD IS ETERNAL LIFE IN CHRIST JESUS, OUR MASTER.

title: Romans 7:1
text: Surely, brothers, you know (for I am speaking to those who know what law means) that law governs a person only during his lifetime?

title: Romans 7:2
text: For a married woman who has a husband is bound by law to her husband during his lifetime; but if her husband dies, she is released from the law of her husband.

title: Romans 7:3
text: So then, if during her husband lifetime, she unites herself with another man, she will be counted an adulteress; but if her husband dies, she is free from the Law, so that she is no adulteress, even if she unites herself with another man.

title: Romans 7:4
text: So also, my brother, you were made dead to the Law through the body of Christ; that you should be joined to another, even to Him who was raised from the dead that we might bear fruit for God.

title: Romans 7:5
text: For while we were unspiritual, the sinful passions, aroused by the Law, were ever active in every part of our bodies, leading us to bear fruit unto death.

title: Romans 7:6
text: But now we have been released from the Law, because we are dead to that in which we were held; so that we are now in thraldom in new and spiritual conditions, and not under the old written code.

title: Romans 7:7
text: What shall we say then? Is the Law sin? Certainly not. On the contrary I should not have become acquainted with sin had it not been for the Law; for except the Law had repeatedly said, "Thou shalt not lust," I should never have known the sin of lust.

title: Romans 7:8
text: But when sin had gained a vantage-ground, by means of the commandment, it stirred up within me all manner of lust; for where there is no law, sin is dead.

title: Romans 7:9
text: Once I lived apart from the Law, myself; but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died;

title: Romans 7:10
text: and the very commandment which should have meant life, this I found to mean death.

title: Romans 7:11
text: For sin, when it had gained a vantage-ground through the commandment, beguiled me, and through it slew me.

title: Romans 7:12
text: So then the Law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good.

title: Romans 7:13
text: Did then that which was good become for me death? Never! but sin did; that it might be manifest as sin, by that the unutterable malignity of sin might become plain through the commandment.

title: Romans 7:14
text: For we know that the Law is spiritual; but as for me, I am a creature of flesh, bought and sold under the dominion of sin.

title: Romans 7:15
text: For what I perform I know not; what I practise is not what I intend to do, but what I detest, that I habitually do.

title: Romans 7:16
text: If then I habitually do what I do not intend to do, I am consenting to the Law, that it is right.

title: Romans 7:17
text: And now it is longer I myself who do the deed, but it is sin which has its home in me.

title: Romans 7:18
text: For I know that in me, that is in my flesh, no good thing has its home; for while to will is present with me, to carry out that which is right is not.

title: Romans 7:19
text: For the good that I intend to do, I do not; but the evil which I do not; but the evil which I do not intend to do, that I am ever practising.

title: Romans 7:20
text: But if I do the very thing I do not intend to do, it is no more I who practise it, but sin which has its home in me.

title: Romans 7:21
text: I find, then, this law, that when I intend to do good, evil is ever present with me.

title: Romans 7:22
text: For in my inmost self I delight in the law of God;

title: Romans 7:23
text: but I find a different law in my bodily faculties, waging war with the law of my will, and taking me prisoner to that law of sin which is in my bodily faculties.

title: Romans 7:24
text: Oh, wretched man that I am! Who shall deliver me from this slave of death?

title: Romans 7:25
text: Oh, thank God! it is through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then I myself in my will am in thraldom to the law of God; yet in my animal nature I am in thraldom to the law of sin.

title: Romans 8:1
text: Thus there is now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus;

title: Romans 8:2
text: for the law of the spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and of death.

title: Romans 8:3
text: For God has done what the Law could not do, weakened as it was by flesh. By sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and on account of sin, he condemned sin in the flesh;

title: Romans 8:4
text: in order that the Law might be fulfilled in us who order our lives not after the flesh, but after the spirit.

title: Romans 8:5
text: For they who live after the flesh, give their attention to the things of the flesh; But they who live after the spirit, give their attention to spiritual things.

title: Romans 8:6
text: To be earthly minded means death; To be spiritually minded means life and peace.

title: Romans 8:7
text: For to be earthly minded is enmity against God; For such a mind is not subject to the Law of God, Nor can it be;

title: Romans 8:8
text: And they who are earthly minded cannot please God.

title: Romans 8:9
text: But you are not earthly, but spiritual, if indeed the Spirit of God is really dwelling in you. If any one does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.

title: Romans 8:10
text: But if Christ is in you, though your bodily self is dead because of sin, your spirit is full of life because of righteousness.

title: Romans 8:11
text: But if the Spirit of Him who raised up Jesus from dead is dwelling in you, He who raised up Jesus from the dead is dwelling in you, He who raised up Christ Jesus from the dead will also make your dying bodily self live by his indwelling Spirit in your lives.

title: Romans 8:12
text: Therefore, brothers, we are debtors-- but not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh;

title: Romans 8:13
text: for if you go on living according to the flesh, you are on the road to die; but if by the Spirit you keep putting to death the deeds of the body, you will live.

title: Romans 8:14
text: For only those are sons of God who are led by God's Spirit.

title: Romans 8:15
text: For you have not received a spirit of slavery in order that you should once more be afraid; but you have received a spirit of adoption, in which we cry out, "My Father, my dear Father!"

title: Romans 8:16
text: For his Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit, that we are children of God;

title: Romans 8:17
text: and if children, then heirs, heirs of God and joint-heirs with Christ; but to share his glory, we must now be sharing his sufferings.

title: Romans 8:18
text: For I count as nothing what we now suffer, in comparison with the glory which will soon be unveiled to us.

title: Romans 8:19
text: All nature even is waiting with eager longing for the unveiling of the vision of God's sons.

title: Romans 8:20
text: For nature was subjected to imperfection, not by its own will, but by the will of Him who thus made it subject--

title: Romans 8:21
text: yet not without the hope that some day nature itself also will be freed from the thraldom of decay, into the freedom which belongs to the glory of the children of God.

title: Romans 8:22
text: For we know that all nature has been groaning and travailing together until this hour.

title: Romans 8:23
text: And not only that, we ourselves, although we are grasping the first-fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves are inwardly groaning, while we are waiting for adoption, the redemption of our body.

title: Romans 8:24
text: For by hope we are saved; but hope which is clearly seen is no longer hope.

title: Romans 8:25
text: Who hopes for what he clearly sees? But if we hope for something that we do not see, we then patiently wait for it.

title: Romans 8:26
text: In the same way the Spirit also takes hold with us in our weakness; for we know knot how to pray as we ought; but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.

title: Romans 8:27
text: And the Searcher of Hearts knows what the Sprit's meaning is, because his intercessions for the saints are according to the will of God.

title: Romans 8:28
text: Now we know that all things continually work together for good to to those who love God, to those who have been the called according to his purpose.

title: Romans 8:29
text: For whom he foreknew, he also foreordained to be conformed to the likeness of his Son, so that he might be the eldest of a great brotherhood;

title: Romans 8:30
text: and whom he foreordained, those he also called; and whom he called, those he also justified; and whom he justified, those he also glorified.

title: Romans 8:31
text: What shall we say then, to these things? If God be for us, Who can be against us?

title: Romans 8:32
text: He that spared not his own Son, But freely delivered him up for us all, How shall he not with him also freely give us all things?

title: Romans 8:33
text: Who shall accuse God's elect? God acquits them;

title: Romans 8:34
text: Who is there to condemn them? Will Christ who died? Yes, and who rose from the dead, The Christ who is also at the right hand of God, And is interceding for us?

title: Romans 8:35
text: What shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall anguish, or calamity, or persecution, or famine? Shall nakedness, or peril, or sword?

title: Romans 8:36
text: Even as it is written: For thy sake we are killed all the day long; We are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.

title: Romans 8:37
text: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors Through Him who loved us.

title: Romans 8:38
text: For I am fully persuaded that neither death nor life, Neither angels nor principalities, nor powers, Neither the present world nor the world to come, Nor the powers of Nature,

title: Romans 8:39
text: Nor height, nor depth, Nor any other created thing, Shall be able to separate us from the love of God Which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

title: Romans 9:1
text: I am speaking the truth in Christ, it is no lie. My conscience bears me witness in the Holy Spirit that I have deep sorrow

title: Romans 9:2
text: and incessant anguish in my heart.

title: Romans 9:3
text: For I was on the point of praying to be accursed from Christ on behalf of my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh.

title: Romans 9:4
text: For they are Israelites; to them belong the sonship, the Shekinah glory, the covenants, the giving of the Law; the service of the temple, and the promises;

title: Romans 9:5
text: theirs are the patriarchs, and of them, as concerning the flesh, is Christ, who is over all, God, blessed forever, Amen.

title: Romans 9:6
text: It is not, however, as though God's word had failed! For they are not all Israel who have sprung from Israel;

title: Romans 9:7
text: they are not all children of Abraham because they are Abraham's descendants. The promise was, In Isaac shall thy posterity be called.

title: Romans 9:8
text: That is, it is not the children of the flesh who are children of God; but the children of the promise are counted as his posterity.

title: Romans 9:9
text: For thus is the word of promise, According to this season I will come, and Sarah shall bear a son.

title: Romans 9:10
text: And not only so, but when Rebecca was pregnant by our forefather Isaac, though one man was the father of both children,

title: Romans 9:11
text: and even though they were still unborn, and had done nothing either good or bad, in order that the purpose of God might stand according to election, not of works, but of Him who called,

title: Romans 9:12
text: it was said to her, The elder shall serve the younger.

title: Romans 9:13
text: As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.

title: Romans 9:14
text: What shall we say then? that there is injustice with God? No indeed.

title: Romans 9:15
text: His words to Moses are: I will have mercy on whom I choose to have mercy; I will have compassion on whom I choose to have compassion.

title: Romans 9:16
text: So then it is not a question of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of God who has mercy.

title: Romans 9:17
text: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, It is for this very purpose that I have raised you up, To show in you my power, And to proclaim my name far and wide, in all the earth.

title: Romans 9:18
text: So then he has mercy on whom he will, and whom he will, he hardens.

title: Romans 9:19
text: Then you will say to me: "Why does he still go on finding fault? Who can withstand his will?"

title: Romans 9:20
text: "Nay, but who are you, O man, that replies to God? Shall the thing formed say unto him who formed it, "Why did you do me like this?"

title: Romans 9:21
text: Or has not the potter power over the clay, to make out of the same lump one vessel for noble, and another for ignoble uses?

title: Romans 9:22
text: But what if God, while intending to show forth his wrath, and to make known his power, yet endured, with much long-suffering, vessels of wrath, fitted to destruction?

title: Romans 9:23
text: And what if he thus purposed to make known the riches of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he had before prepared for glory?

title: Romans 9:24
text: Now such are we whom he has called, not only from among the Jews, but also from among the Gentiles.

title: Romans 9:25
text: As he also said in Hosea: Those who were not my people I will call "my people," And her "beloved" who was not beloved;

title: Romans 9:26
text: And in that very spot where it was told them, "You are not my people," There they shall be called "Sons of the living God."

title: Romans 9:27
text: And in regard to Israel, Isaiah exclaims: Though the number of the sons of Israel be like the sands of the sea, it is but a remnant of those who shall be saved;

title: Romans 9:28
text: for the Lord will execute his word upon the earth, finishing it and cutting it short.

title: Romans 9:29
text: Even as in an earlier passage, Isaiah says, Except the Lord of Sabbath had us some few descendants, we should have become like Sodom, and should have fared like Gomorrah.

title: Romans 9:30
text: What then shall we say? That Gentiles who never pursed righteousness have overtaken it, even the righteousness of faith?

title: Romans 9:31
text: But that the descendants of Israel, who were in pursuit of a law of righteousness, did not arrive at that law?
