title: Romans 9:32
text: And why? Because they sought it not by faith, but thought to gain it by works. They stumbled at the stone of stumbling;

title: Romans 9:33
text: even as it is written: Behold, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; but he that believes on Him shall not be put to shame.

title: Romans 10:1
text: Brothers, the longing of my heart and my prayer to God is for my countrymen, that they may be saved.

title: Romans 10:2
text: For I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, only it is a zeal without knowledge.

title: Romans 10:3
text: For because they were ignorant of God's righteousness, and sought to establish their own righteousness, they did not submit themselves to the righteousness of God.

title: Romans 10:4
text: For to every believer Christ is an end of law as a means of righteousness.

title: Romans 10:5
text: For Moses writes concerning the righteousness of the Law, saying, The man that doeth it shall live by it.

title: Romans 10:6
text: But the righteousness of faith speaks in this way: Say not in thine heart, "Who shall ascend to heaven?"-- that is, to bring Christ down;

title: Romans 10:7
text: nor,"Who shall descend into the abyss?"-- that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.

title: Romans 10:8
text: But what does it say? The word is near thee, even in thy mouth and in thy heart. That is the very word of faith which we preach;

title: Romans 10:9
text: Confess with your mouth "Jesus is Lord," and believe in your heart that God actually raised him from the dead, and you will be saved.

title: Romans 10:10
text: For with the heart man believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

title: Romans 10:11
text: The Scriptures say, Whoever believes in Him will not be put to shame.

title: Romans 10:12
text: For there is no difference between Jew and Gentile, because the same Lord Jesus is all over, and is rich unto all who call upon Him;

title: Romans 10:13
text: for Whoever will call upon the name of the Lord will be saved.

title: Romans 10:14
text: How then shall thy call upon Him in whom they do not believe? And how are they to believe in One of whom they have never heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher?

title: Romans 10:15
text: And how can men preach unless they are sent? As it is written, How beautiful are the feet of those who bring a glad gospel.

title: Romans 10:16
text: And yet they did not all hearken to the good news; for Isaiah said, Lord, who hath believed our message?

title: Romans 10:17
text: So faith comes from a message heard, and the message comes from the teaching of Christ.

title: Romans 10:18
text: But I ask, Did they fail to hear? Yes, truly, Their sound has gone out unto all the earth, And their words unto the ends of the world.

title: Romans 10:19
text: But I say, Did Israel not know? First Moses says: I will provoke you to jealousy with that which is no nation; Against a Gentile nation, void of understanding, will I anger you.

title: Romans 10:20
text: But Isaiah speaks very boldly, I was found of those who were not seeking me, I was made manifest to those who were not asking for me.

title: Romans 10:21
text: But to Israel he says, All day long I have been spreading out my hands unto a disobedient and contrary people.

title: Romans 11:1
text: Then I ask, Did God cast off his people? No indeed. For I also am an Israelite, a son of Abraham, a member of the tribe of Benjamin.

title: Romans 11:2
text: God did not cast off his people whom he foreknew. For do you not know what is said in the Scripture about Elijah? how he pleaded with God against Israel, saying,

title: Romans 11:3
text: Lord, they have killed thy prophets, they have overthrown thine altars; And now I alone am left, and they seek my life.

title: Romans 11:4
text: But what was the answer of God to him? I have reserved for myself seven thousand who have not bowed the knee to Baal.

title: Romans 11:5
text: In the same way also at this time there is a remnant chosen by gift of grace.

title: Romans 11:6
text: But if it is by grace, it is no longer of works; or else grace is no more grace.

title: Romans 11:7
text: What then? that which Israel has been seeking for, that he has not obtained; but the chosen have obtained it, and the rest have been hardened.

title: Romans 11:8
text: According as it is written, God has given them a spirit of slumber, Eyes that they should not see, Ears that they should not hear, unto this day.

title: Romans 11:9
text: As David says: Let their table be made a snare and a trap, And a stumbling-block and a recompense unto them;

title: Romans 11:10
text: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, And bow thou down their backs forever.

title: Romans 11:11
text: I ask then, "Have they stumbled so as to fall?" No indeed; but by their lapse salvation has come unto Gentiles, "to provoke Israel to jealousy."

title: Romans 11:12
text: Now if their stumbling enriches the world, and their loss enriches the Gentiles, how much more must their fulness do!

title: Romans 11:13
text: For to you who are Gentiles I say that since I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I glorify my ministry,

title: Romans 11:14
text: if by any means I might "provoke to jealousy" my kinsmen, and save some among them.

title: Romans 11:15
text: For if their casting out is the reconciliation of the world to God, what will their restoration be but life out of death?

title: Romans 11:16
text: Now if the first-fruits of the dough [Abraham and the Patriarchs] are holy, so also is the whole mass [their descendants]. And if the root of a tree [Abraham] is holy, so also are the branches [his descendants].

title: Romans 11:17
text: Supposing that some of the branches have been broken off, and you, although you were but a wild olive, have been grafted in among the branches and have become a partaker with them of the fatness of the olive tree, do not glory over the branches;

title: Romans 11:18
text: or if you are glorying, remember that it is not you who uphold the root, but the root which upholds you.

title: Romans 11:19
text: "Branches have been broken off," you say, "that I might be grafted in."

title: Romans 11:20
text: True, through their unbelief they were broken off, and by your faith you stand. Do not be puffed up, but fear;

title: Romans 11:21
text: for if God spared not the natural branches, neither will he spare you.

title: Romans 11:22
text: Fix your gaze, therefore, on the goodness and the severity of God; towards those who fell, severity, but towards you, God's goodness, if you continue stedfast in his goodness; otherwise you, too, will be cut off.

title: Romans 11:23
text: And they also [those Jews], if they do not continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in again; for God is able to graft them in again.

title: Romans 11:24
text: For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a mere wild olive tree, and have been grafted, contrary to nature, into a fruitful olive tree, how much more shall these, the natural branches, be regrafted into their own olive tree?

title: Romans 11:25
text: For I would not, my brothers, have you ignorant of this hidden truth, for fear that you become wise in your own conceits: that a hardening in part has befallen Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles is come in.

title: Romans 11:26
text: And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written: The deliver will come from Zion, He will banish all ungodliness from Jacob;

title: Romans 11:27
text: This is my covenant with them, When I shall take away their sins.

title: Romans 11:28
text: In relation to the gospel, the Jews are God's enemies for your sake; but in relation to the election, they are dearly loved for their forefather's sake.

title: Romans 11:29
text: For no change of purpose can annul God's free gift and call.

title: Romans 11:30
text: And as in times past you were yourselves disobedient to God, but now, thanks to their disobedience, have obtained mercy;

title: Romans 11:31
text: even so they also have now been disobedient, that by the mercy shown to you they also may now obtain mercy.

title: Romans 11:32
text: For God has locked up all in the prison of disobedience, that upon all he may have mercy.

title: Romans 11:33
text: Oh, the depths of the riches, both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unfathomable are his judgments, and how unsearchable his paths!

title: Romans 11:34
text: Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counsellor?

title: Romans 11:35
text: Who has first given to Him, So as to receive payment in return?

title: Romans 11:36
text: For of him and through him, and for him, are all things. All glory to him forever and ever! Amen.

title: Romans 12:1
text: I entreat you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies to Him as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God. This is your reasonable service of worship.

title: Romans 12:2
text: And be not conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your minds, so that you may prove what is the good and acceptable and perfect will of God.

title: Romans 12:3
text: For, through the grace that was given to me, I tell every man among you not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but so to think, as to think soberly, according to the measure of faith which God has given him.

title: Romans 12:4
text: For even as we have many members in one body, and not all members have the same function;

title: Romans 12:5
text: so we, who are many, are one body in Christ, and we are severally members of one another.

title: Romans 12:6
text: But we have gifts differing according to the grace which was given to us. He that has the gift of prophecy, let him prophesy according to the proportion of his faith.

title: Romans 12:7
text: If it is the gift of administration, let us give ourselves to our service.

title: Romans 12:8
text: Let the teacher give himself to his teaching; and he who exhorts others to his exhortation. He who gives, let him do it in singleness of mind. He who rules, let him rule with diligence; and he who shows mercy must be cheerful.

title: Romans 12:9
text: Let love be without insincerity. Abhor what is evil; wed yourselves to what is good.

title: Romans 12:10
text: As for brotherly love, be tenderly affectionate one to another, in honor preferring one another.

title: Romans 12:11
text: In your diligence be free from sloth. Be glowing in spirit. Slave for the master.

title: Romans 12:12
text: Rejoice in hope; be patient under affliction; continue stedfast in prayer.

title: Romans 12:13
text: Be liberal to needy saints. Practise hospitality.

title: Romans 12:14
text: Bless your persecutors, bless, and curse not.

title: Romans 12:15
text: Rejoice with those who rejoice, and weep with those who weep.

title: Romans 12:16
text: Have full sympathy with one another. Set not your minds on high affairs, but associate with lowly folk. Do not be wise in your own conceits.

title: Romans 12:17
text: Do not pay back evil for evil. Aim to do what is honorable in the eyes of all.

title: Romans 12:18
text: If it be possible, so far as it lies with you, be at peace with all men.

title: Romans 12:19
text: Never revenge yourself, beloved, but leave the field clear for God's wrath; for it is written, "Vengeance is mine, I will repay," says the Lord.

title: Romans 12:20
text: On the contrary, therefore, If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink; for by so doing you will be heaping burning coals on his head.

title: Romans 12:21
text: Do not be overcome by evil, but be overcoming evil with good.

title: Romans 13:1
text: Every one should be in the higher authorities; for there is no authority apart from God. The authorities that now exist have been appointed by God.

title: Romans 13:2
text: Therefore the man who rebels against authority is opposing the divine ordinances; and those who withstand will bring judgment on themselves.

title: Romans 13:3
text: For rulers are no terror to good deeds, but to evil. Would you be fearless of the ruler's authority? Do what is good, and you will have his praise.

title: Romans 13:4
text: For the ruler is God's minister appointed for your good. But if you are a wrong-doer, be afraid; he does not carry the sword to no purpose; he is God's servant, appointed to vengeance upon the guilty.

title: Romans 13:5
text: Wherefore you must needs be in subjection, not only because of fear, but also for conscience sake.

title: Romans 13:6
text: This too, is the reason why you pay taxes; because the authorities are ministers of God's service, attending continually upon this very thing.

title: Romans 13:7
text: Render to all their dues; taxes to whom taxes, customs to whom customs, respect to whom respect, and homage to whom homage is due.

title: Romans 13:8
text: Never owe any one anything save the debt of brotherly love; for he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the Law.

title: Romans 13:9
text: For the Law which says, Thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt do no murder, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not bear false witness, thou shalt not covet, and whatever other commandment there be--is all summed up in this one saying, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.

title: Romans 13:10
text: Love never wrongs his neighbor; therefore love is the fulfilment of the Law.

title: Romans 13:11
text: Carry out these injunctions because you know the crisis that we are in, that now it is high time for you to awake out of sleep; for now is our salvation nearer than when we first believed.

title: Romans 13:12
text: The night is far spent; The day is at hand. Let is therefore take off the deeds of darkness, Let us put on the armor of light.

title: Romans 13:13
text: Let us live honestly, as in the day, Not in reveling and drunkenness, Not in lust and licentiousness, Not is strife and jealousy;

title: Romans 13:14
text: But clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, And make no provisions for your earthly nature And the gratification of its lusts.

title: Romans 14:1
text: Welcome a man of weak faith, but not for the purpose of deciding doubtful points.

title: Romans 14:2
text: One man has faith to eat anything; but he whose faith is weak, eats only vegetables.

title: Romans 14:3
text: He who eats meat must not despise the man who abstains; and let not the man who abstains judge him who eats; for God has received him.

title: Romans 14:4
text: Who are you just that judges the household-servant of another? To his own lord he stands or falls. And stand he will, for his Master has power to make him stand.

title: Romans 14:5
text: There are some who esteem one day above another; there are others who esteem all days alike; let each other be fully persuaded in his own mind.

title: Romans 14:6
text: He who regards the day, regards it unto his Lord; and he who regards it not, disregards it unto his Lord. He who eats meat, eats unto his Lord, for he gives God thanks; and he who abstains, abstains unto his Lord, since he, too, gives God thanks.

title: Romans 14:7
text: For not one of us lives unto himself, and not one dies unto himself.

title: Romans 14:8
text: If we live, we live unto our Lord; if we die, we die unto our Lord. So then, whether we live or die, we belong to our Lord.

title: Romans 14:9
text: For this purpose Christ died and became alive again, that he might be the Lord both of the dead and of the living.

title: Romans 14:10
text: But you [the abstainer], why do you pass judgment on your brother? Or you again [the non-abstainer], why do you despise yours? For we shall all stand before the judgment-seat of God.

title: Romans 14:11
text: For it is written, "As I live," says the Lord, "to me every knee shall bow, And to God shall every tongue confess."

title: Romans 14:12
text: So then each one of us shall give account of himself to God.

title: Romans 14:13
text: So let us no longer pass judgment on one another; rather let this be your judgment, that no one put a stumbling-block in his brother's way, nor any cause of falling.

title: Romans 14:14
text: I know and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is in itself unclean; but any food is "unclean" for one who considers it "unclean."

title: Romans 14:15
text: If your brother is continually pained because of your food, you are not conducting yourself any longer in love. Do not, by what you eat, persist in destroying a man for whom Christ died.

title: Romans 14:16
text: Therefore do not let what is right, so far as you are concerned, be evil spoken of.

title: Romans 14:17
text: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.

title: Romans 14:18
text: Those who are slaving for Christ devotedly in these ways, are well pleasing to God and highly commended by man.

title: Romans 14:19
text: So then let is eagerly pursue the things that make for peace and the upbuilding of each other.

title: Romans 14:20
text: Do not, for the sake of food, be tearing down God's work. All food indeed is ceremonially clean, but a man is in the wrong if his food proves a stumbling-block.

title: Romans 14:21
text: The right course is not to eat meat, nor to drink wine, nor to do anything through which your brother is made to stumble.

title: Romans 14:22
text: Have you faith? Keep it to yourself as in the presence of God. He is a happy man who does not condemn himself in that which he approves.

title: Romans 14:23
text: But he who has misgivings, and yet eats meat, is condemned already, because his action is not based on faith; and whatever is not based on faith is sin.

title: Romans 15:1
text: Now we who are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to seek our own pleasure.

title: Romans 15:2
text: Let each one of us try to make his neighbor happy for his good, unto his upbuilding.

title: Romans 15:3
text: For even Christ pleased not himself; but as it is written, The reproaches of those who were reproaching thee fell upon me.

title: Romans 15:4
text: For everything that was written of old has been written for our instruction, that through patience, and through the comfort of the Scriptures, we might have hope.

title: Romans 15:5
text: Now the God of patience and of comfort grant you to be in full sympathy with one another, in accordance with the example of Jesus Christ;

title: Romans 15:6
text: so that with one heart and with one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

title: Romans 15:7
text: Wherefore always receive one another into fellowship, to the glory of God, even as Christ also received you.

title: Romans 15:8
text: For I say that Christ has been made a minister of the Circumcision [the people of Israel], in vindication of God's truth, so that he may confirm the promises given to our forefathers;

title: Romans 15:9
text: and so that the Gentiles also should praise God for his mercy, as it is written, Therefore I will offer praise to thee among the Gentiles, And sing to thy name.

title: Romans 15:10
text: Or again, Rejoice, O Gentiles, with his people.

title: Romans 15:11
text: Or again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles, And let all the people extol him.

title: Romans 15:12
text: Or again, as Isaiah says: There shall be the root of Jesse, And he that arises to rule over the Gentiles; On him shall the Gentiles hope.

title: Romans 15:13
text: Now the God of all hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may be overflowing with hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: Romans 15:14
text: And I myself also am confident regarding you, my brothers, that you yourselves are already full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and well able to give advice to one another.

title: Romans 15:15
text: Still I have written unto you the more boldly, in part, by way of reminding you, because of that gift of grace which God bestowed upon me, in making me a priest of Jesus Christ unto the Gentiles.

title: Romans 15:16
text: I act as priest of the gospel of God; so that the Gentiles, when offered before him, may be an acceptable sacrifice, because consecrated by the Holy Spirit.

title: Romans 15:17
text: I have then my boast in Christ Jesus concerning the things of God.

title: Romans 15:18
text: For I will not dare to speak of any thing except that which Christ has done through me to bring the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed,

title: Romans 15:19
text: through the might of signs and wonders, in the power of the Holy Spirit. So that beginning at Jerusalem and its environs, I have proclaimed without reserve the gospel of Christ, even as far as Illyricum.

title: Romans 15:20
text: My ambition has been, however, to preach the gospel where Christ's name was not already known, so that I might not build upon another man's foundation.

title: Romans 15:21
text: But, as Scripture says, He shall be seen by those to whom no news about him ever came, And those who have never heard of him shall understand.

title: Romans 15:22
text: This is why I have been so hindered from coming to you.

title: Romans 15:23
text: But now, since I have no more any "opening" in these parts, and since I have longed for many years to come to you

title: Romans 15:24
text: whenever I go to Spain, I am hoping to see you on my way there, and to be set forward by you on my way there, and to be set forward by you on my journey thither, after I have enjoyed your company for a little while.

title: Romans 15:25
text: Just now I am going to Jerusalem to serve the saints.

title: Romans 15:26
text: For it has been the good pleasure of Macedonia and Achaia to make an offering for the poor among the saints at Jerusalem.

title: Romans 15:27
text: Yes, it has been made their good pleasure, and their debt, too. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual riches, they owe it to them also to minister to them [the Jews] in worldly goods.

title: Romans 15:28
text: When, therefore, I have settled this, and have secured to them [the poor at Jerusalem] the fruit of this collection, I shall come on by you into Spain.

title: Romans 15:29
text: And I know that when I come to you, I shall come in the fulness of the blessing of Christ.

title: Romans 15:30
text: Brothers, I beseech you, by Jesus Christ our Lord, and by the love which the Spirit gives, to help me in my struggle by your prayers to God on my behalf,

title: Romans 15:31
text: that I may be delivered from the disobedient in Judea; that my mission to Jerusalem may be favorably received by the saints;

title: Romans 15:32
text: and that I may come to you in joy, by the will of God, and find rest together with you.

title: Romans 15:33
text: The God of peace be with you all! Amen.

title: Romans 16:1
text: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, who is a minister of the church at Cenchrae.

title: Romans 16:2
text: I beg you to give her a Christian welcome, as the saints should; and to assist her in any matter in which she may have need of you. For she herself has been made an overseer to many people, including myself.

title: Romans 16:3
text: Salute Priscilla and Aquila, my fellow laborers in the cause of Jesus Christ,

title: Romans 16:4
text: who risked their own lives to save mine; who are thanked not only by me,

title: Romans 16:5
text: but by all the churches among the Gentiles. Salute likewise the church that meets in their home. Salute Epaenetus, my dearly beloved, the first man in Roman Asia to believe in Christ.

title: Romans 16:6
text: Salute Mary, who toiled terribly for you;

title: Romans 16:7
text: and Andronicus and Junia, my kinsfolk and fellow prisoners, who are notable among the apostles, and who became Christians before I did.

title: Romans 16:8
text: Salute Amplias, my beloved in the Lord;

title: Romans 16:9
text: and Urbanus, my fellow toiler in Christ; and Stachys, my dear, dear friend.

title: Romans 16:10
text: Salute Apellas, tested and tried in Christ, and the household of Aristobulus,

title: Romans 16:11
text: and Herodion, my kinsman. Salute the believing members of the household of Narcissus.

title: Romans 16:12
text: Salute Trypheana and Tryphosa, who are ever toiling in the Lord. Salute dear Persis, who has toiled terribly in the Lord's service.

title: Romans 16:13
text: Salute Rufus, the chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

title: Romans 16:14
text: Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are associated with them.

title: Romans 16:15
text: Salute Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, Olympas, and all the saints associated with them.

title: Romans 16:16
text: Salute one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ salute you.

title: Romans 16:17
text: I exhort you, brothers, to keep watch of those who are causing the divisions among you, and occasions of stumbling, contrary to the teaching which you have learned.

title: Romans 16:18
text: Turn away from them. For men of that stamp are not the slaves of Christ, but are slaves to their own appetites. By their smooth and fair speech they beguile the hearts of the innocent.

title: Romans 16:19
text: I say this, for the tidings of your obedience have been told throughout the world. On your own behalf, then, I rejoice; but I want you to be wise unto the good, but innocents in evil.

title: Romans 16:20
text: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

title: Romans 16:21
text: Timothy, my fellow worker, salutes you; so do my fellow countrymen Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater.

title: Romans 16:22
text: I, Tertius, who write this letter, salute you in the Lord.

title: Romans 16:23
text: Gaius, my host, and the host of the church, salutes you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, salutes you, and so does brother Quartus.

title: Romans 16:24
text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all!

title: Romans 16:25
text: Now I commend you to Him who is able to keep you stedfast, according to my gospel, and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, whereby is unveiled the secret truth which was kept secret through immemorial ages,

title: Romans 16:26
text: but now has been brought to light, and by command of the eternal God made known to the Gentiles by the scriptures of the Prophets, so that the Gentiles might hold obedience of the faith.

title: Romans 16:27
text: Unto Him, the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, be glory forever. Amen.

title: I Corinthians 1:1
text: Paul, called by the will of God to be an apostle of Jesus Christ, and Sosthenes, his brother:

title: I Corinthians 1:2
text: to the Church of God at Corinth, to those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, together with all, wherever they are, who call upon the name of the Lord Jesus:

title: I Corinthians 1:3
text: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

title: I Corinthians 1:4
text: I am always thanking God on your behalf, for the grace of God bestowed on you in Christ Jesus;

title: I Corinthians 1:5
text: that in everything you have been enriched in him, in all speech, and in all knowledge

title: I Corinthians 1:6
text: (for thus my witness for Christ was confirmed among you);

title: I Corinthians 1:7
text: so that you lack no divine gift, while you are waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.

title: I Corinthians 1:8
text: He will also keep you perfectly stedfast unto the end, so that you will be unreprovable in the Day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

title: I Corinthians 1:9
text: Faithful is the God by whom you were called into fellowship with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

title: I Corinthians 1:10
text: Now I beg you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to speak in accord, all of you, and to have no divisions among you, but to be knit together in a common mind and temper.

title: I Corinthians 1:11
text: For it has been plainly told me concerning you, my brothers, by Chloe's people, that there are dissensions among you.

title: I Corinthians 1:12
text: I mean by this that one of you says, "I am a follower of Paul"; another, "I of Apollos"; another, "I of Cephas"; another, "I of Christ."

title: I Corinthians 1:13
text: Has Christ been divided? Paul, was he crucified for you? or was it into the name of Paul that you were baptized?

title: I Corinthians 1:14
text: I am thankful to God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,

title: I Corinthians 1:15
text: so that no one can say you were baptized in my name.

title: I Corinthians 1:16
text: Yes, I did baptize the house of Stephanas also, but I do not think I baptized any one else.

title: I Corinthians 1:17
text: For Christ did not think I baptized any one else. For Christ did not send me forth to baptize, but to proclaim the gospel; and that not in philosophic words, lest the Cross of Christ should be made an empty thing.

title: I Corinthians 1:18
text: For the message of the Cross is indeed for those on their way to destruction, foolishness; but for us who are on our way to salvation it is the power of God.

title: I Corinthians 1:19
text: For thus it is written, I will destroy the wisdom of the philosophers, And the prudence of the prudent will I confound.

title: I Corinthians 1:20
text: Sage, rabbi, skeptic of this present age--where are they all? Has not God made foolish the philosophy of the world?

title: I Corinthians 1:21
text: For when, in the wisdom of God, the world by its philosophy knew not God, the world by its philosophy knew not God, it pleased God, by the foolishness of preaching, to save those who believe.

title: I Corinthians 1:22
text: Jews continue to ask for miracles and Greeks are ever wanting philosophy,

title: I Corinthians 1:23
text: but we come preaching a crucified Messiah--to Jews a stumbling-block, to Greeks foolishness,

title: I Corinthians 1:24
text: but to those who are the called, whether Jews or Greeks, Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God.

title: I Corinthians 1:25
text: For the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.

title: I Corinthians 1:26
text: For consider your own calling, brothers, that not many wise in earthly wisdom, not many powerful, not many of noble birth, have been called.

title: I Corinthians 1:27
text: No, God has chosen the world's folly to confound its philosophy; and the world's weakness to confound its strength.

title: I Corinthians 1:28
text: The world's base things has God chosen, and the things that are not, to bring to naught the things that are;

title: I Corinthians 1:29
text: so that no mortal man should glory in his presence.

title: I Corinthians 1:30
text: It is of him that you are in Christ Jesus, whom God made unto us wisdom and righteousness and sanctification and redemption,

title: I Corinthians 1:31
text: so that as Scripture says, He that glories, let him glory in the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 2:1
text: And when I came to you, brothers, I came not to proclaim God's great secret purpose in fine language of philosophy;

title: I Corinthians 2:2
text: for I determined to know nothing, while among you, but Jesus as Christ, and him a crucified Christ.

title: I Corinthians 2:3
text: In weakness and fear and great trembling came I among you.

title: I Corinthians 2:4
text: My message and my preaching were not in the persuasive language of philosophy, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power;

title: I Corinthians 2:5
text: in order that your faith should rest, not on human philosophy, but on the power of God.

title: I Corinthians 2:6
text: Notwithstanding, among those who are mature I do teach philosophy; though not the philosophy of the present age, nor of its rulers who are coming to nought.

title: I Corinthians 2:7
text: No, it is God's wisdom that I utter, that hidden wisdom which God had decreed before the world began, unto our glory.

title: I Corinthians 2:8
text: None of the rulers of the present age understands it, for if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of Glory.

title: I Corinthians 2:9
text: Nay, as it is written: Eye has not seen, Nor ear heard, Neither have entered into man's heart The things which God has prepared For those who love him.

title: I Corinthians 2:10
text: Yet God has unveiled them to us by his Spirit. For the Spirit fathoms everything, even the abysmal depths of God.

title: I Corinthians 2:11
text: For what man knows the depths of man except the man's own inner Spirit? Even so, also, the Spirit of God knows the deeps profound of God.

title: I Corinthians 2:12
text: But we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which comes forth from God, that we may realize the blessings freely given us by God.

title: I Corinthians 2:13
text: Of these high themes we speak in words not taught by human philosophy, but by the Spirit; interpreting spiritual things to spiritual men.

title: I Corinthians 2:14
text: The unspiritual man rejects the teachings of God's Spirit; for him it is folly. He cannot understand it, for it is spiritually discerned,

title: I Corinthians 2:15
text: But the spiritual man discerns everything, yet is himself discerned by no one.

title: I Corinthians 2:16
text: For what man understands the mind of the Lord, that he should instruct Him?

title: I Corinthians 3:1
text: As for me, brothers, I could not talk to you as spiritual men, but as to creatures of flesh, mere babes in Christ.

title: I Corinthians 3:2
text: I fed you milk, not meat; for you were unable to bear it.

title: I Corinthians 3:3
text: You are not able even now, for you are still unspiritual. While there is among you jealousy and strife, are you not still unspiritual, and behaving like worldlings?

title: I Corinthians 3:4
text: When one says, "I follow Paul," and another, "I follow Apollos," are you not mere worldlings?

title: I Corinthians 3:5
text: What then is Apollos? What is Paul? Just ministers through whom you have believed, and each doing the work that the Lord gave him.

title: I Corinthians 3:6
text: I planted, Apollos watered, but God made the seed grow.

title: I Corinthians 3:7
text: So neither is he who planted anything, nor he who watered, but God alone, who is making the seed grow.

title: I Corinthians 3:8
text: Now, though he who plants and he who waters are one, each will receive his own reward, according to his own service.

title: I Corinthians 3:9
text: For we are God's fellow workers; and you are God's field, you are God's building.

title: I Corinthians 3:10
text: According to the grace of God vouchsafed me, like a skillful master-builder, I have laid a foundation; but another will be building upon it. Let each take heed how he builds on it.

title: I Corinthians 3:11
text: The foundation is already laid--Jesus Christ--and no man can lay another.

title: I Corinthians 3:12
text: On that foundation, if a man proceeds to build gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble, each man's work will be made manifest.

title: I Corinthians 3:13
text: The Day will disclose it, for it dawns in fire, and the fire will test each man's work, of what quality it is.

title: I Corinthians 3:14
text: If any man's work--the building he has made--stands the test, he will be rewarded.

title: I Corinthians 3:15
text: If any man's work is burned up, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, as it were through the flames.

title: I Corinthians 3:16
text: Do you not know what you are God's sanctuary, and that the Spirit of God is dwelling within you?

title: I Corinthians 3:17
text: If any one tear down God's sanctuary, God will tear him down; for the sanctuary of God is holy, and that is what you are.

title: I Corinthians 3:18
text: Let no one deceive himself. If any one of you supposes that he is wise in the philosophy of the present age, let him become foolish, so that he may be wise.

title: I Corinthians 3:19
text: For the philosophy of this world is foolishness in God's sight. It is written, He snares the wise in their own craftiness,

title: I Corinthians 3:20
text: and again, The Lord knows the reasonings of the wise, how futile they are.

title: I Corinthians 3:21
text: So let no one make boast in men. For all things are yours;

title: I Corinthians 3:22
text: Paul, Apollos, Cephas, the world, life, death, things present or things to come; all things are yours;

title: I Corinthians 3:23
text: and you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.

title: I Corinthians 4:1
text: Let any man look upon us as servants of Christ, and stewards of the secret truths of God.

title: I Corinthians 4:2
text: Now it is required of stewards, that a man be found faithful.

title: I Corinthians 4:3
text: But to me it matters very little that I am judged by you, or by any earthly court.

title: I Corinthians 4:4
text: Indeed I do not even judge myself; for though I know nothing against myself, yet that does not vindicate me; for he who judges me is the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 4:5
text: So make no hasty judgment until the Lord come, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make plain the purpose of men's hearts. Then each man's due praise will come to him from God.

title: I Corinthians 4:6
text: Now these things, brothers, I have applied in a figure to myself and to Apollos for your sakes; that in us you might learn not to go beyond what is written; that none of you be puffed up for the one, against the other.

title: I Corinthians 4:7
text: For who makes you a differ, brother? Or what have you that you did not receive? But if you did receive it, why are you boasting as if you had not received it?

title: I Corinthians 4:8
text: But you, forsooth, are already full, are you? You are already rich? Without us you are already reigning? Yes, and I would that you did reign, so that we also might reign with you.

title: I Corinthians 4:9
text: But it seems to me that God has exhibited us apostles, last of all, like men doomed to death; for we are made a spectacle to the whole world, both to men and to angels.

title: I Corinthians 4:10
text: For Christ's sake we are fools, but you are quite philosophic in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong; you are honorable, but we are outcast.

title: I Corinthians 4:11
text: Even to his very hour we are enduring hunger and thirst and nakedness and blows.

title: I Corinthians 4:12
text: Homeless men, we toil, working with our own hands.

title: I Corinthians 4:13
text: When reviled, we bless; when persecuted, we endure; when defamed, we conciliate. We have been made, as it were, scum-o'-the-earth, the very refuse of the world, to this very hour!

title: I Corinthians 4:14
text: I am not writing this to shame you, but to admonish you, as my beloved children.

title: I Corinthians 4:15
text: For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ Jesus, you can have but one father. For in Christ Jesus I begot you through the gospel.

title: I Corinthians 4:16
text: I beg you then to imitate my example.

title: I Corinthians 4:17
text: With this in mind I have sent Timothy to you. He is my dear and faithful son in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Christ; the manner in which I ever teach everywhere in every church.

title: I Corinthians 4:18
text: Now some are puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.

title: I Corinthians 4:19
text: But come to you I will, and that soon, if it please the Lord, and then I shall learn not the talk of these boasters, but their power.

title: I Corinthians 4:20
text: For the kingdom of God is not in talk, but in power.

title: I Corinthians 4:21
text: Which do you want? Am I to come to you with a rod, or in a loving and tender spirit?

title: I Corinthians 5:1
text: It is actually reported that there is immorality among you, and such immorality as is not even among the heathen--that a man has taken his father's wife!

title: I Corinthians 5:2
text: Yet you are puffed up instead of mourning and removing from among you the man who has done this thing.

title: I Corinthians 5:3
text: For I, although absent in body, yet present in spirit, have already passed sentence, by the authority of our Lord Jesus Christ, on him who has done this thing.

title: I Corinthians 5:4
text: When you are gathered together, and my spirit is with you together with the power of our Lord Jesus,

title: I Corinthians 5:5
text: I have handed over such a man to Satan for the destruction of his flesh, that his spirit may be saved, in the day of the Lord Jesus.

title: I Corinthians 5:6
text: Your glorying is not good. Do you not know that even a little leaven leavens all the lump?

title: I Corinthians 5:7
text: Then get rid of the old leaven, so that you may be like a new lump, as you are now unleavened. For our Paschal Lamb has already been sacrificed, Christ himself.

title: I Corinthians 5:8
text: So let us keep the unending feast, not with any old leaven, neither with leaven of malice and vice, but with unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

title: I Corinthians 5:9
text: I told you in my letter not to associate with the immoral.

title: I Corinthians 5:10
text: Not that in this world you were actually to have no contact with the immoral, the avaricious, the thievish, or with idolaters; for then you would have to leave the world, altogether.

title: I Corinthians 5:11
text: But what I wrote was that you were not to associate with any so-called brother who is immoral, or avaricious, or idolatrous, or abusive, or a drunkard, or an extortioner. No, with such persons do not even sit at table.

title: I Corinthians 5:12
text: What have I to do with the judging of outsiders? Must not you judge those who are within the church, while God judges outsiders?

title: I Corinthians 5:13
text: Expel that wicked man from among you.

title: I Corinthians 6:1
text: Dare any one of you who has a grievance against his neighbor go to law before heathen judges, instead of before the saints?

title: I Corinthians 6:2
text: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is to be tried by you, are you unfit to try such trifling cases?

title: I Corinthians 6:3
text: Do you not know that we are to try angels? How much more, then, the affairs of life.

title: I Corinthians 6:4
text: Why then, if you have cases relating to earthly affairs which need to be decided, is it men who are absolutely nothing in the church whom you make your judges?

title: I Corinthians 6:5
text: I say this to shame you. Is it so that there is not among you a single wise man, capable of deciding between a man and his brother?

title: I Corinthians 6:6
text: Must brother go to law with brother, and that, too, before unbelievers?

title: I Corinthians 6:7
text: Indeed, to say nothing more, the fact that you have lawsuits with one another is altogether a defect in you. Why not rather suffer injustice? Why not rather endure being cheated?

title: I Corinthians 6:8
text: On the contrary, you yourselves are inflicting injustice and fraud, and that upon your brothers.

title: I Corinthians 6:9
text: Do you not know that the wicked will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived. None who are immoral, or idolaters, or adulterers, or catamites, or sodomites,

title: I Corinthians 6:10
text: or thieves, or avaricious men, or drunkards, or foul-mouthed men, or extortioners will inherit the kingdom of God.

title: I Corinthians 6:11
text: Such were some of you, but you have washed away your stains, you have been consecrated, you have been justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, and in the Spirit of our God.

title: I Corinthians 6:12
text: "All things are lawful for me"? Yes, but not all things are good for me. "All things are lawful for me"? Yes, but I will not let myself be enslaved by the power of any.

title: I Corinthians 6:13
text: "Food is meant for the stomach, and the stomach for food"? Yes, but God will soon put an end both to the one and to the other. The body, however, exists not for immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body;

title: I Corinthians 6:14
text: and the God who raised up our Lord will up-raise us also by his mighty power.

title: I Corinthians 6:15
text: You know, do you not, that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them members of a harlot? God forbid!

title: I Corinthians 6:16
text: Do you not know that he who joins himself to a harlot is one with her in body? (For God says, The two shall become one flesh.)

title: I Corinthians 6:17
text: While a man who is united with the Lord is one with Him in spirit?

title: I Corinthians 6:18
text: Flee from immorality. Every [other] sin that a man commits lies outside the body, but the immoral man sins against his own body.

title: I Corinthians 6:19
text: Do you not know that your body is a sanctuary of the Holy Spirit who is within you, the Spirit whom you have from God?

title: I Corinthians 6:20
text: You are not your own; for you have been bought with a price, therefore glorify God in your bodies.

title: I Corinthians 7:1
text: Now concerning the question in your letter. It is well for a man to have no intercourse with a woman,

title: I Corinthians 7:2
text: but because there is so much immorality let each man have his own wife; and let each women have her own husband.

title: I Corinthians 7:3
text: Let the husband give his wife her due, and likewise the wife her husband. The wife is not mistress of her own person,

title: I Corinthians 7:4
text: but her husband is; and in the same way the husband is not master of his own person, but his wife is.

title: I Corinthians 7:5
text: Do not refuse one another, unless it is only temporary and by mutual consent, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer. Then come together again, lest through your lack of self-control Satan begin to tempt you to sin.

title: I Corinthians 7:6
text: But what I have just said is by way of concession, not command.

title: I Corinthians 7:7
text: I would that every one lived as I do; but each man has his own special gift from God, one this, another that.

title: I Corinthians 7:8
text: But to the unmarried, and the widows, I say that it is well for them to remain as I am.

title: I Corinthians 7:9
text: If, however, they are not exercising self-control, by all means let them marry; for marriage is better than the fever of passion.

title: I Corinthians 7:10
text: But to those already married my commandment is--and not mine, but the Lord's--that a wife is not to leave her husband;

title: I Corinthians 7:11
text: (or if she has already left him let her either remain as she is, or be reconciled to him), and also that a husband is not to put away his wife.

title: I Corinthians 7:12
text: To the rest it is I who am speaking, not the Lord. If any brother has a wife who is not a believer, if he is willing to live with her, let him not send her away.

title: I Corinthians 7:13
text: And a woman whose husband is not a believer, if he is willing to live with her, let her not separate from him.

title: I Corinthians 7:14
text: For the unbelieving husband is consecrated through union with his believing wife; and the unbelieving wife, through union with her believing husband. Otherwise your children would be unholy, but now they are consecrated to God.

title: I Corinthians 7:15
text: But if the unbelieving partner be determined to leave, separation let it be. In such cases the believing husband or wife is not under bondage. But it is into peace that God has called us.

title: I Corinthians 7:16
text: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

title: I Corinthians 7:17
text: Only whatever be the lot in life to which God has assigned each one--and whatever the condition in which he was living when God called him--in that let him continue. Such is the rule I give in all the churches.

title: I Corinthians 7:18
text: So, was any man called, being circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Was any man called when he was uncircumcised? Let him not be circumcised.

title: I Corinthians 7:19
text: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God's commands in everything.

title: I Corinthians 7:20
text: Whatever be the condition of life in which he was called, in that let him continue.

title: I Corinthians 7:21
text: Were you called in slavery? Let not that trouble you; but if you can become free make use of the opportunity.

title: I Corinthians 7:22
text: For the slave who has been called in the Lord is the Lord's freedman; and in the same way, the free man who is called is Christ's slave.

title: I Corinthians 7:23
text: You have been brought with a price; do not become slaves to men.

title: I Corinthians 7:24
text: Where each man stood when he was called, there, brothers, let him stay, close to God.

title: I Corinthians 7:25
text: I have no command from the Lord to give you concerning unmarried women; but I give you my opinion, and it is that of a man who, through the Lord's mercy, is deserving of your confidence.

title: I Corinthians 7:26
text: I think then, that in view of the time of suffering now imminent, it is best for a man to remain as he is.

title: I Corinthians 7:27
text: Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be free. Are you free from the marriage bond? Do not seek for a wife.

title: I Corinthians 7:28
text: Yet if you do not marry, you have not done wrong; and if a girl marries, she has not done wrong. Such people, however, will have trouble in worldy affairs, and I wish to spare you.

title: I Corinthians 7:29
text: Indeed, brothers, the time that remains to us has been shortened; so let those who have wives live as if they had none,

title: I Corinthians 7:30
text: let those who weep be as though they did not weep, those who rejoice as though they did not rejoice, those who buy as though they did not possess,

title: I Corinthians 7:31
text: and those who use the world as though using it sparingly. For the present phase of the world is passing away.

title: I Corinthians 7:32
text: So I want you to be free from all anxieties. An unmarried man is anxious about the Lord's business, how he may please the Lord;

title: I Corinthians 7:33
text: but a married man is anxious about worldly affairs, how he may please his wife, and he is divided in his mind.

title: I Corinthians 7:34
text: Again, the woman who is widow, or the maid, is anxious about the Lord's business, how she may be pure in body and in mind; but the married woman is anxious about worldly affairs, how she may please her husband.

title: I Corinthians 7:35
text: It is in your own interest that I say this; not that I may entangle you in a snare, but that I may help you to serve the Lord with fitting and undistracted service.

title: I Corinthians 7:36
text: If, however, a father feels that he is not treating his virgin daughter in a seemly manner, in leaving her unmarried beyond the flower of her age, and so the matter is urgent, let him do what she desires; he commits no sin. Let the marriage take place.

title: I Corinthians 7:37
text: On the other hand, he who is firm in his purpose and is under no compulsion, but is free to carry out his own wishes, and who has determined to keep his daughter unmarried, does well.

title: I Corinthians 7:38
text: So he that gives his daughter in marriage is doing right, and he who keeps her unmarried will be doing right, and he who keeps her unmarried will be doing better.

title: I Corinthians 7:39
text: A wife is bound to her husband during his lifetime; but if her husband dies, she is free to marry whomever she will, provided it be in the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 7:40
text: But she is happier, in my judgment, if she remains as she is; and I think that I, too, have the Spirit of God.

title: I Corinthians 8:1
text: Now in regard to food which has been offered to idols, we are sure of course that "we all have knowledge." But knowledge puffs up, while love builds up.

title: I Corinthians 8:2
text: If a man thinks that he already has knowledge, he does not yet truly know as he ought to know;

title: I Corinthians 8:3
text: but if a man loves God, he is known by him.

title: I Corinthians 8:4
text: Now as to eating food that has been offered to idols, we know well that an idol has no real existence in the universe, and that there is no God but One.

title: I Corinthians 8:5
text: For though there be so-called "gods," celestial of terrestrial, as indeed there are gods many and lords many,

title: I Corinthians 8:6
text: yet for there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things, and we for him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.

title: I Corinthians 8:7
text: But that "knowledge" is not possessed by all; but some, accustomed until now to the idol, eat food as that which has actually been offered to an idol, and so their conscience, being still weak, is defiled.

title: I Corinthians 8:8
text: Now food does not bring us nearness to God. Neither if we eat do we gain any advantage, nor if we eat not, do we lose any.

title: I Corinthians 8:9
text: But see to it lest this right of yours become a stumbling-block to the weak.

title: I Corinthians 8:10
text: For if any one should see you, the possessor of "knowledge," reclining at table in an idol's temple, would not his conscience, if he were weak, be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols?

title: I Corinthians 8:11
text: So he is lost, this weak man, lost by your "knowledge." this brother for whom Christ died.

title: I Corinthians 8:12
text: In so sinning against your brothers, and in ever and again wounding their weak consciences, you are sinning against Christ.

title: I Corinthians 8:13
text: Therefore, if what I eat makes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, lest I make my brother to stumble.

title: I Corinthians 9:1
text: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?

title: I Corinthians 9:2
text: Even if I am not an apostle to others, to you at least I am; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 9:3
text: This is my reply to my critics.

title: I Corinthians 9:4
text: Have I no right to claim food and drink?

title: I Corinthians 9:5
text: Have I no right to take a believing wife with me on my journey, as the rest of the apostles and the Lord's brothers and Peter do?

title: I Corinthians 9:6
text: Are we the only ones, Barnabas and I, who have no right to give up manual labor?

title: I Corinthians 9:7
text: What soldier ever serves at his own expense? What farmer ever plants a vineyard and his flock and does not taste the milk?

title: I Corinthians 9:8
text: Am I saying this on human authority only, or does not the Law also say the same?

title: I Corinthians 9:9
text: Yea, in the Law of Moses it is written, Thou shalt not muzzle an ox while he is treading out the grain.

title: I Corinthians 9:10
text: Is it the oxen that God is thinking about, or is it really said for our sakes? It was written for us; because the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the thresher in hope of getting a share of the crop.

title: I Corinthians 9:11
text: If I have sown for you the seeds of spiritual good, is it a great thing if I reap from you temporal goods?

title: I Corinthians 9:12
text: If others share this authority over you, do not I far more? Yet I have not availed myself of it, but am patiently enduring; so that I may not in any way hinder the progress of Christ's gospel.

title: I Corinthians 9:13
text: You know, do you not, that those who minister in the temple, and those who serve at the altar, get their portion of the sacrifices?

title: I Corinthians 9:14
text: Even so the Lord ordained that those who proclaim the gospel should get their living by the gospel.

title: I Corinthians 9:15
text: But for my part, I have never availed myself of any of these rights. I do not say this to bring it about in my own case. I would rather die than let any one make void this boast of mine.

title: I Corinthians 9:16
text: Proclaiming the gospel gives me no ground of boasting; for necessity is laid upon me; woe is me if I preach not the gospel.

title: I Corinthians 9:17
text: For if I do this of my own accord, I have my pay; but if unwilling, I have at least discharged my stewardship.

title: I Corinthians 9:18
text: What then is my wage? This, that I can make the gospel free where I carry it; and that I can refrain from using my rights as a preacher of the gospel.

title: I Corinthians 9:19
text: Though free from all men, I make myself the slave of all, that I may win the more.

title: I Corinthians 9:20
text: To the Jews I am become like a Jew, that I may win Jews; to those under the Law, like one under the Law, though I am not under the Law, myself;

title: I Corinthians 9:21
text: to those outside the Law, as one outside the Law, to win those outside the Law (though I am not outside the law of God, but inside the law of Christ).

title: I Corinthians 9:22
text: I am become weak to the weak, to win the weak. I am become all these things to all men that, by any and by all means, I may save some.

title: I Corinthians 9:23
text: And I am doing it all for the gospel's sake, that I may become a copartner in it.

title: I Corinthians 9:24
text: Do you not know that in a foot-race, though all run, only one receives the prize? So run that you may win.

title: I Corinthians 9:25
text: Every man who contends in the games continually trains himself by all manner of self-restraint. Now they do it to get a fading garland, but we, one that is unfading.

title: I Corinthians 9:26
text: For my part, then, I run with no wavering to the goal. I box not as one beating the air,

title: I Corinthians 9:27
text: but I bruise my body and keep it in subjection, lest having called others to the contest, I should myself be disqualified.

title: I Corinthians 10:1
text: For I would not have you ignorant, brothers, how our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea,

title: I Corinthians 10:2
text: and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.

title: I Corinthians 10:3
text: They all ate of the same spiritual bread,

title: I Corinthians 10:4
text: and all drank from the same spiritual stream, for they were drinking from a spiritual rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ.

title: I Corinthians 10:5
text: But in most of them God was not well pleased, for they were laid low in the desert.

title: I Corinthians 10:6
text: Now this happened as a warning for us, that we might not long for evil things as they longed.

title: I Corinthians 10:7
text: And you must not be idolaters like some of them: as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, And they rose up for idol dances.

title: I Corinthians 10:8
text: Nor must we act licentiously, as some of them did, and fell in a single day, twenty-three thousand of them.

title: I Corinthians 10:9
text: Neither must we presume upon the patience of our Lord, as some of them presumed, and were destroyed by the serpents;

title: I Corinthians 10:10
text: nor murmur, as some of them did, and were destroyed by the Destroying Angel.

title: I Corinthians 10:11
text: Now these things were happening to them typically, but were written down for our admonition who stand at the meeting of the ages.

title: I Corinthians 10:12
text: So then let him who imagines that he is standing so securely beware lest he fall.

title: I Corinthians 10:13
text: No temptation has overtaken you that is beyond man's power; but God is faithful, who will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear, but will, with every temptation, provide the way of escape also, so that you may be able to withstand.

title: I Corinthians 10:14
text: So then, my beloved, continually flee from idolatry.

title: I Corinthians 10:15
text: I am speaking to men of sense; do you yourselves judge what I say.

title: I Corinthians 10:16
text: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not a common participation in the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not a common participation in the body of Christ?

title: I Corinthians 10:17
text: Because we who are many are one bread, one body, for we all do share in the one loaf.

title: I Corinthians 10:18
text: Look at Israel according to the flesh; are not those who eat the sacrifices in communion with the altar?

title: I Corinthians 10:19
text: What then shall we say? that an offering to an idol is anything? or that an idol is really anything?

title: I Corinthians 10:20
text: On the contrary, what the heathen sacrifice they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I do not want you to have communion with demons.

title: I Corinthians 10:21
text: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and also the cup of demons; you cannot be partakers in the Lord's table and in the table of demons.

title: I Corinthians 10:22
text: What! would we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?

title: I Corinthians 10:23
text: "All things are lawful," you say? But not all things are expedient; "all things are lawful"; but not all build up.

title: I Corinthians 10:24
text: Let not each one be always seeking his own, but rather his neighbor's good.

title: I Corinthians 10:25
text: Eat anything that is for sale in the markets, asking no questions for conscience sake;

title: I Corinthians 10:26
text: for the earth and its fulness are the Lord's.

title: I Corinthians 10:27
text: If one who is not a believer invites you to his house, and you wish to go, eat everything that is set before you, without asking questions for conscience sake.

title: I Corinthians 10:28
text: But if any one tells you, "This food has been offered in sacrifice," do not eat it, for the sake of him who told you,

title: I Corinthians 10:29
text: and for your conscience sake--his conscience, not your own. "But," you may object, "why should my freedom be decided upon another's scruples of conscience?

title: I Corinthians 10:30
text: If I eat after giving thanks, why am I denounced for eating that for which I have given thanks?"

title: I Corinthians 10:31
text: Because whether you are eating or whether you are drinking, you are to do it all for the glory of God.

title: I Corinthians 10:32
text: Do not be a cause of stumbling either to Jews of to Gentiles, or to the church of God.

title: I Corinthians 10:33
text: For so I also try to please all men in every way, not by seeking my own good, but the good of the many, that they may be saved.

title: I Corinthians 11:1
text: Be imitators of me, as I am an imitator of Christ.

title: I Corinthians 11:2
text: Indeed I praise you for remembering me in everything, and because you are holding fast to the traditions just as you received them.

title: I Corinthians 11:3
text: But I wish you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and of a wife her husband is head; and that God is head of Christ.

title: I Corinthians 11:4
text: Every man who prays or prophesies with head veiled dishonors his Head;

title: I Corinthians 11:5
text: but every woman who prays or prophesies with her head unveiled dishonors her head (her husband): for it is one and the same thing as if she were shaven.

title: I Corinthians 11:6
text: If a woman does not wear a veil, let her also cut off her hair; now if it is a disgrace for a woman to have her hair cut off or her head shaved, let her be veiled.

title: I Corinthians 11:7
text: A man, indeed, ought not to have his head veiled, for he is an image and glory of God; but woman is a glory of man.

title: I Corinthians 11:8
text: For it is not man who was made from woman, but woman was made from man.

title: I Corinthians 11:9
text: And man was not created for woman, but woman for man.

title: I Corinthians 11:10
text: For this reason the woman ought to have authority over her head, because of her [guardian] angels.

title: I Corinthians 11:11
text: However, in the Lord neither is woman independent of man, nor is man independent of woman;

title: I Corinthians 11:12
text: for just as the woman was made from the man, so also is the man born of the woman, while they both come from God.

title: I Corinthians 11:13
text: Judge of this for your own selves. It is fitting that a woman should pray to God with her head unveiled.

title: I Corinthians 11:14
text: Nor does nature itself teach you that it is a disgrace to a man to have long hair,

title: I Corinthians 11:15
text: but it is woman's glory, because her hair has been given her instead of a veil.

title: I Corinthians 11:16
text: If, however, any one is inclined to be disputatious regarding such a custom, let him know that neither I nor the churches of God hold to such a custom.

title: I Corinthians 11:17
text: But in giving you the following instructions, I cannot praise you; your solemn assemblies do more harm than good.

title: I Corinthians 11:18
text: To begin with, I am told--and I believe there is some truth in it--that when you meet at a church there are divisions among you.

title: I Corinthians 11:19
text: For there must needs be also parties among you, in order that the good may be tested and made known.

title: I Corinthians 11:20
text: Again, when you meet together, there is no true eating of the Lord's Supper;

title: I Corinthians 11:21
text: for each one of you begins to eat his own supper; one goes hungry, while another gets drunk.

title: I Corinthians 11:22
text: What! Have you no houses in which to eat or drink? or do you wish to show your contempt for the church of God, and to shame those who have no homes to eat in? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this I certainly do not praise you.

title: I Corinthians 11:23
text: For I passed on to you the account, which I myself received from the Lord; how the Lord Jesus, on the very night he was betrayed, took bread,

title: I Corinthians 11:24
text: and when he had given thanks, he broke it, saying, "This is my body, broken for you; this do in memory of me."

title: I Corinthians 11:25
text: In the same way also, he took the cup after supper, saying: "This cup is the new covenant in my blood; do this, whenever you drink it, in memory of me."

title: I Corinthians 11:26
text: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you are proclaiming your Lord's death until he come.

title: I Corinthians 11:27
text: So he that eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthy must answer for a sin against the body and blood of the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 11:28
text: Let each man scrutinize himself, and thus let him eat of the bread and drink of the cup.

title: I Corinthians 11:29
text: For whoever eats and drinks without discerning the body, eats and drinks condemnation to himself.

title: I Corinthians 11:30
text: This is why many among you are feeble and sickly, and many sleep.

title: I Corinthians 11:31
text: If however, we were judging ourselves aright, we should not now be condemned;

title: I Corinthians 11:32
text: but through our condemnation by the Lord, we are trained so that we may not be condemned;

title: I Corinthians 11:33
text: So, my brothers, whenever you come together for this meal, wait for one another.

title: I Corinthians 11:34
text: If any one is hungry, let him eat at home, so that your meetings do not bring condemnation upon you. The other matters I will adjust when I come.

title: I Corinthians 12:1
text: Now concerning spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not wish you to be ignorant.

title: I Corinthians 12:2
text: You know that when you were heathen you went astray after dumb idols, wherever he be led.

title: I Corinthians 12:3
text: Wherefore I want you to understand that no one who speaks in the Spirit of God says, "Jesus is accursed," and no one can say, "Jesus is Lord," except in the Holy Spirit.

title: I Corinthians 12:4
text: Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit;

title: I Corinthians 12:5
text: there are various forms of service, and the same Lord;

title: I Corinthians 12:6
text: and varieties of work, and the same God, who works in all.

title: I Corinthians 12:7
text: Now to each man has been given his manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.

title: I Corinthians 12:8
text: For to one man by the Spirit has been given a word of wisdom, to another a word of insight by the same Spirit;

title: I Corinthians 12:9
text: to one man by the same Spirit is given faith, to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit;

title: I Corinthians 12:10
text: to another the powers which work miracles, to another prophecy, to another the discernment of spirits; to another varieties of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues.

title: I Corinthians 12:11
text: But the one and the same Spirit gives power to all, distributing his gifts to each as he wills.

title: I Corinthians 12:12
text: For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, although they be many, are one body; so also is Christ.

title: I Corinthians 12:13
text: And we can see this, for in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jew or Gentile, whether slave or free, and we were all made to drink of one Spirit.

title: I Corinthians 12:14
text: For the body is not one member, but many.

title: I Corinthians 12:15
text: If the foot should say, "Because I am a hand, I am not part a part the body," would it not indeed be a part of the body?

title: I Corinthians 12:16
text: Or if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I am not a part of the body," would it be any less a part of the body?

title: I Corinthians 12:17
text: If the whole body were an eye, where were hearing? If all were hearing, where were smelling?

title: I Corinthians 12:18
text: But now God has set the members, each one of them, in the body as it has pleased him.

title: I Corinthians 12:19
text: If all were one member, where would the body be?

title: I Corinthians 12:20
text: But now there are many members, but one body.

title: I Corinthians 12:21
text: And the eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you": nor again of head to the feet, "I have no need for you."

title: I Corinthians 12:22
text: On the contrary, we need those members of the body which seem to be weaker;

title: I Corinthians 12:23
text: upon those parts of the body which we esteem less honorable, we bestow more abundant honor, and our uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness.

title: I Corinthians 12:24
text: For whereas our comely parts have no need, God has tempered the body together, giving more abundant honor to that member in which lacked;

title: I Corinthians 12:25
text: that there should be no disunion in the body, but that members mutual care for one another.

title: I Corinthians 12:26
text: When one member suffers, all the others suffer with it; and when one member is honored, all the members are glad with it.

title: I Corinthians 12:27
text: Now you are the body of Christ, and individually members of it.

title: I Corinthians 12:28
text: And God has appointed those in the church to be first of all apostles, second, prophets, third, teachers: then workers of miracles, healers, helpers, administrators, users of various kinds of "tongues."

title: I Corinthians 12:29
text: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? teachers? workers of miracles?

title: I Corinthians 12:30
text: Have all gifts of healing? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret?

title: I Corinthians 12:31
text: Desire earnestly the greater gifts. And yet I will go on to show you a still more excellent way.

title: I Corinthians 13:1
text: Though I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have no love, I am become a clanging brass, or a clashing cymbal.

title: I Corinthians 13:2
text: Though I have the gift of prophecy and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

title: I Corinthians 13:3
text: And though I sell all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it avails me nothing.

title: I Corinthians 13:4
text: Love suffers long and is kind; love envies not; love makes no parade, is not puffed up,

title: I Corinthians 13:5
text: is not rude, nor selfish, nor easily provoked. Love bears no malice, never rejoices over wrong-doing,

title: I Corinthians 13:6
text: but rejoices when the truth rejoices.

title: I Corinthians 13:7
text: It knows how to be silent, it is trustful, hopeful, patient, enduring.

title: I Corinthians 13:8
text: Love never fails; but though there are prophecies, they will fail; though there are tongues, they will cease; though there is knowledge, it will be superseded.

title: I Corinthians 13:9
text: For our knowing is imperfect, and our prophesying is imperfect;

title: I Corinthians 13:10
text: but when the perfect is come, then the perfect will be done away.

title: I Corinthians 13:11
text: When I was a child I spoke like a child, felt like a child, thought like a child; now that I am become a man, I have done with childish things.

title: I Corinthians 13:12
text: For now we see as in a mirror, and are baffled, but then face to face; now I know in fragments, but then shall I understand even as I also have been understood.

title: I Corinthians 13:13
text: Faith, Hope, Love endure--these three; but the greatest of these is Love.

title: I Corinthians 14:1
text: Hotly pursue this love, yet seek earnestly spiritual gifts, and chiefly that you may prophesy.

title: I Corinthians 14:2
text: For he who speaks in a "tongue" speaks not to man but to God, for no one understands him, but in the Spirit he utters secret truths.

title: I Corinthians 14:3
text: But he who prophesies addresses words to men that build up, encourage, and console.

title: I Corinthians 14:4
text: He who speaks in a tongue upbuilds himself; but he who prophesies upbuilds the church.

title: I Corinthians 14:5
text: Now I should like you all to speak with "tongues"; but I should rather that you prophesied, For he who prophesies is greater than he who speaks with tongues, unless he interprets, so that the church may be built up.

title: I Corinthians 14:6
text: Now brothers, if I should come to you speaking with tongues, what should I benefit you, unless I speak to you some revelation, or knowledge, or prophecy, or teaching?

title: I Corinthians 14:7
text: For if lifeless instruments such as the flute or the harp give no distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is fluted or harped?

title: I Corinthians 14:8
text: Or, for example, if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, what soldier will be prepared for battle?

title: I Corinthians 14:9
text: In the same way with you, if you utter unintelligible words with your tongue, how can what you say be understood? You will be speaking to the winds!

title: I Corinthians 14:10
text: There are, let us say, so many languages in the world, and none without its meaning.

title: I Corinthians 14:11
text: If then I do not know the force of expression, I shall seem a barbarian to the one who uses it, and he will seem a barbarian to me.

title: I Corinthians 14:12
text: So also in your case, since you are ambitious for spiritual gifts, seek to excel in them for the upbuilding of the church.

title: I Corinthians 14:13
text: So let him who speaks with tongues pray that he may interpret.

title: I Corinthians 14:14
text: For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is barren.

title: I Corinthians 14:15
text: What then? I will pray with my spirit, and I will pray also with my mind. I will praise God with my spirit, but I will praise him with my mind, also.

title: I Corinthians 14:16
text: For if you in your spirit bless God, how shall he who fills the place of the unlearned say the Amen to your thanksgiving, when he does not know what you are talking about?

title: I Corinthians 14:17
text: You on the one hand offer a good thanksgiving, but the other is not built up.

title: I Corinthians 14:18
text: Thank God I speak with tongues more than you all,

title: I Corinthians 14:19
text: but in the church I would rather speak five words with my understanding, so as to instruct others, than ten thousand in an unknown tongue.

title: I Corinthians 14:20
text: Brothers, do not become children in understanding; be babes in malice, but in understanding become mature men.

title: I Corinthians 14:21
text: In the Law it is written. With men of other tongues, and by the lips of strangers, will I speak to this people, and even then they will not listen to me, says the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 14:22
text: So then the gift of tongues is for a sign, not to believers, but to unbelievers; but prophecy is not for unbelievers, but for those who believe.

title: I Corinthians 14:23
text: Accordingly, when the whole church assemblies, and everybody is speaking "with tongues," if there enter men unlearned or unbelieving, will they not say that you are mad?

title: I Corinthians 14:24
text: But if all are prophesying when an unlearned or unbelieving man enters, he is convicted in conscience by your speaker, he feels himself judged by all,

title: I Corinthians 14:25
text: and the secret depths of his heart are laid open. So he will fall upon his face and worship God, saying, "Of a truth, God is with you."

title: I Corinthians 14:26
text: What follows, then, brothers? Whenever you meet together, each contributes something; a psalm, a sermon, a revelation, a tongue, an interpretation. Let all be done for edification.

title: I Corinthians 14:27
text: If any one speaks in an unknown tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three, and that in turn, and let some one interpret.

title: I Corinthians 14:28
text: But if there is no one to interpret, let them keep silence in the church, and speak to themselves and to God.

title: I Corinthians 14:29
text: Let the prophets speak by two or three, and let the others exercise their judgment.

title: I Corinthians 14:30
text: But if to one as he sits there some revelation is made, let the first be silent.

title: I Corinthians 14:31
text: For you can all prophesy one by one; so that all may be learning, and all may be encouraged.

title: I Corinthians 14:32
text: The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets,

title: I Corinthians 14:33
text: for God is not a God of confusion, but of peace. This custom prevails in all the churches of the saints.

title: I Corinthians 14:34
text: "In your congregation" [you write], "as in all the churches of the saints, let the women keep silence in the churches, for they are not permitted to speak. On the contrary let them be subordinate, as also says the law.

title: I Corinthians 14:35
text: And if they want to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a women to speak in church."

title: I Corinthians 14:36
text: What, was it from you that the word of God went forth, or to you only did it come?

title: I Corinthians 14:37
text: If any one thinks himself a prophet or spiritual, let him recognize that what I am now writing you is a command of the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 14:38
text: But if any one disregard it he will be disregarded.

title: I Corinthians 14:39
text: So, my brothers, be ambitious for the gift of prophecy, and speak not against the gifts of tongues.

title: I Corinthians 14:40
text: Let everything be done decently and in order.

title: I Corinthians 15:1
text: Now I am calling to your remembrance, brothers, the gospel which I preached to you, which you also received, and on which you have taken your stand,

title: I Corinthians 15:2
