text: So also noble deeds are conspicuous, and even if otherwise, they cannot be kept hidden.

title: I Timothy 6:1
text: Let those who are under the yoke as slaves esteem their masters as worthy of all honor, so that the name of God and the teachings be not blasphemed.

title: I Timothy 6:2
text: Those whose masters are Christian believers must not treat them with disrespect, because they are brothers; nay, rather slave for them the better because those who get the benefit of their services are believing and beloved. Continue to teach and preach this.

title: I Timothy 6:3
text: If any one teaches heterodoxy, and refuses to consent to the wholesome words of the Lord Jesus Christ, and to the teachings of religion,

title: I Timothy 6:4
text: he is puffed up with conceit and knows nothing, but is doting about disputations and a strife of words. These give rise to envy, quarrels, railings, evil suspicions,

title: I Timothy 6:5
text: and wrangling between men whose minds are corrupt and destitute of the truth; who suppose that godliness is a source of gain.

title: I Timothy 6:6
text: Now godliness with contentment is truly gainful;

title: I Timothy 6:7
text: for we have brought nothing into the world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out!

title: I Timothy 6:8
text: So if we have food and shelter, let us be content with that.

title: I Timothy 6:9
text: Those who desire to be rich fall into the snares of temptation and many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.

title: I Timothy 6:10
text: For the love of money is a source of all kinds of evil; and in their eager desire to be rich some have been led astray form the faith, and have pierced themselves with many sorrows.

title: I Timothy 6:11
text: But you, O servant of God, flee from these things, and run after integrity, piety, faith, love, stedfastness, gentleness.

title: I Timothy 6:12
text: Keep contending in the noble contest of the faith; seize hold on eternal life, to which you were called when you confessed the good confession in the presence of many witnesses.

title: I Timothy 6:13
text: In the presence of God who gives life to all, and of Christ Jesus who bore witness to the good confession before Pontius Pilate,

title: I Timothy 6:14
text: I charge you, keep your commission spotless and irreproachable until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.

title: I Timothy 6:15
text: For in his own good time this will be brought about by that blessed and only potentate, King of kings and Lord of lords,

title: I Timothy 6:16
text: who alone possesses immortality, who dwells in light that none can approach, whom no man has ever seen or can see; to whom be honor and power everlasting. Amen.

title: I Timothy 6:17
text: Charge the rich of this world not to be supercilious, nor to trust in uncertain riches, but in God, who provides all things richly for our use.

title: I Timothy 6:18
text: Charge them to practise benevolence, to be rich in good works, to be open-handed and generous,

title: I Timothy 6:19
text: laying up right good treasure for themselves in the world to come, in order that they may obtain the Life which is life indeed.

title: I Timothy 6:20
text: O, Timothy, guard the treasure which is committed to you. Shun the profane babblings and contradictions of the falsely called "knowledge"

title: I Timothy 6:21
text: which some professing have erred from the faith. Grace be with you.

title: II Timothy 1:1
text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, by the will of God, sent forth to proclaim the promise of the life which is in Christ Jesus:

title: II Timothy 1:2
text: To Timothy, my beloved child; Grace mercy, and peace to you from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

title: II Timothy 1:3
text: I give thanks to God whom I worship with a pure conscience as my fathers did, when I remember you unceasingly in my prayers.

title: II Timothy 1:4
text: Night and day when I recall your tears I am longing to see you, that my happiness may be complete.

title: II Timothy 1:5
text: I have been reminded of that sincere faith which is in your heart; which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice, and, I am fully persuaded, dwells in you also.

title: II Timothy 1:6
text: For this reason let me remind you to keep ever blazing that gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands.

title: II Timothy 1:7
text: For God has not given us a spirit of cowardice, but a spirit of power and of love and of self-control.

title: II Timothy 1:8
text: Do not then be ashamed to bear witness for our Lord, nor for me, his prisoner. Nay, join with me in suffering for the gospel by the power of God.

title: II Timothy 1:9
text: He has saved us and called us with a holy calling, not dealing with us according to our works , but according to his purpose and grace which he gave us in Christ Jesus before the beginning of time.

title: II Timothy 1:10
text: This has now been made manifest through the appearing of our Saviour Christ Jesus, who has put an end to death, and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.

title: II Timothy 1:11
text: Of the gospel I was appointed a herald, apostle, and teacher; and that is the reason I am now undergoing these sufferings.

title: II Timothy 1:12
text: But I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have fully believed, and I am thoroughly persuaded that he is able to keep what I have given him until the Day.

title: II Timothy 1:13
text: Hold fast the pattern of sound teaching you have heard from me in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.

title: II Timothy 1:14
text: Guard the glorious trust which has been committed to you by the aid of the Holy Spirit who makes his home in us.

title: II Timothy 1:15
text: You already know that all the Christians in Roman Asia forsook me, among them Phygellus and Hermogenes.

title: II Timothy 1:16
text: The Lord show mercy to the house hold of Onesiphorus; for many a time he refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain.

title: II Timothy 1:17
text: But when he came to Rome he sought for me until he found me.

title: II Timothy 1:18
text: The Lord grant him to find mercy form the Lord in that Day! And you know better than I how many services he rendered in Ephesus.

title: II Timothy 2:1
text: Do you then, my son, strengthen you heart in the grace which is in Christ Jesus.

title: II Timothy 2:2
text: The teachings which you have heard from me, attested by many witnesses, deliver into the keeping of faithful men, who in their turn will be able to teach others also.

title: II Timothy 2:3
text: Take your share in suffering as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.

title: II Timothy 2:4
text: A soldier in active service avoids entangling himself in the every-day affairs of life, so that he may please his commander.

title: II Timothy 2:5
text: And again, an athlete is not crowned unless he obeys the rules of the game.

title: II Timothy 2:6
text: The farmer who has done the work should be the first to get a share of the crop.

title: II Timothy 2:7
text: Reflect on what I am telling you. The Lord will give you understanding in everything.

title: II Timothy 2:8
text: Always remember that Jesus Christ, a descendant of David, has been raised from the dead according to the gospel I proclaim.

title: II Timothy 2:9
text: For preaching it I am suffering, and am even put in chains as a malefacter.

title: II Timothy 2:10
text: But God's message is no prisoner. That is why I endure everything for the sake of the chosen, that they also may obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.

title: II Timothy 2:11
text: Faithful is the saying: "If we have died with him, we shall also live with him.

title: II Timothy 2:12
text: If we endure suffering, we shall also reign with him. If we disown him, he too will disown us.

title: II Timothy 2:13
text: If we prove faithless. he abides faithful, for he cannot be false to himself."

title: II Timothy 2:14
text: Always call these truths to men's mind; adjuring them in the presence of God to avoid controversy. It is a useless thing, and subverts those who listen to it.

title: II Timothy 2:15
text: Strive earnestly to present yourself unto God, tested and proved worthy by trial, a workman unashamed, ever cutting a straight path for the message of the truth.

title: II Timothy 2:16
text: but avoid profane babble; for people will go farther and farther in impiety,

title: II Timothy 2:17
text: and their teaching will spread like a gangrene.

title: II Timothy 2:18
text: Among such are Hymenaeus and Philetus, who have gone astray concerning the truth by declaring that the resurrection is already past; and they are undermining the faith of some.

title: II Timothy 2:19
text: Nevertheless God's firm foundation stands unshaken, bearing this inscription, THE LORD KNOWS THOSE WHO ARE HIS, and this also, LET EVERY ONE WHO NAMES THE NAME OF THE LORD RENOUNCE WICKEDNESS.

title: II Timothy 2:20
text: Now in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay, some for noble, some for ignoble uses.

title: II Timothy 2:21
text: If then a man keeps himself clear of these latter, he will be a vessel for honor, consecrated, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work.

title: II Timothy 2:22
text: Flee from the passions of youth, but run after righteousness, faith, love, and peace, in company with those who out of a pure heart call upon the Lord.

title: II Timothy 2:23
text: Ever shun foolish and puerile discussions, for you know that they lead to quarrels.

title: II Timothy 2:24
text: The Lord's slave must not quarrel, but must be kind to all men; a skilful teacher, patient of wrong.

title: II Timothy 2:25
text: He must be gentle when instructing opponents; for possibly God may give them a change of mind for the recognition of the truth,

title: II Timothy 2:26
text: and they may come to their senses again, and escape the snare of the devil, as they are restored to life by God to do his will.

title: II Timothy 3:1
text: But of this be sure: In the last days grievous times will come.

title: II Timothy 3:2
text: For men will be selfish, mercenary, boastful, haughty, blasphemous, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, irreligious,

title: II Timothy 3:3
text: without natural affection, merciless, slanderous, dissolute, and brutal.

title: II Timothy 3:4
text: They will hate goodness, they will be treacherous, reckless, blinded with pride, lovers of pleasure, rather than lovers of God.

title: II Timothy 3:5
text: For although they keep up the outward form of religion, they deny its power.

title: II Timothy 3:6
text: Turn away from all such. Some of them creep into private houses and lead captive silly women who, laden with sins,

title: II Timothy 3:7
text: and led captive by ever-changing impulses, are always learning but never able to arrive at knowledge of truth.

title: II Timothy 3:8
text: As Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so also do these men withstand the truth; being corrupt in mind and worthless in all that concerns the faith.

title: II Timothy 3:9
text: But they will not get on; for their folly will be made as openly manifest to all as was that of Jannes and Jambres.

title: II Timothy 3:10
text: But you, Timothy, have followed my teaching, my conduct, my aims, my faith, patience, love, endurance,

title: II Timothy 3:11
text: as well as the persecutions and sufferings which befell me at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. You know all the persecutions I endured, and how the Lord delivered me out of them all!

title: II Timothy 3:12
text: Yes, and all who purpose to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.

title: II Timothy 3:13
text: But wicked men and impostors will go on from bad to worse, deceiving others, and being themselves deceived.

title: II Timothy 3:14
text: But do you hold fast what you have learned and have held to be true. You know those from whom you have learned it,

title: II Timothy 3:15
text: and how from a child you have known the Holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise unto salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.

title: II Timothy 3:16
text: Every Scripture, seeing that it is God-breathed, is also profitable for teaching, for refutation, for correction, and for training in righteousness,

title: II Timothy 3:17
text: so that the man of God may himself be complete, and completely equipped for every good work.

title: II Timothy 4:1
text: I adjure you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus who is about to judge the living and the dead-- by his appearing and his kingdom, I adjure you--

title: II Timothy 4:2
text: proclaim the message, be urgent in season and out of season; convince, rebuke, encourage, with never-failing patience and teaching.

title: II Timothy 4:3
text: For a time will come when they will not listen to wholesome teaching, but wanting to have their ears tickled, they will heap up for themselves teachers upon teachers to satisfy their own fancies.

title: II Timothy 4:4
text: They will turn away their ears from the truth, and turn aside to myths.

title: II Timothy 4:5
text: But as for you, be always self-controlled, face hardships, do the work of a missionary, discharge all the duties of your ministry.

title: II Timothy 4:6
text: I for my part am a libation already being poured in sacrifice; and the time of my unmooring is at hand.

title: II Timothy 4:7
text: I have fought in the glorious contest; I have run the race; I have kept the faith.

title: II Timothy 4:8
text: Henceforth there is laid up for me the garland of righteousness which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will award to me on that Day, and not to me only, but also to all those who have loved his appearing.

title: II Timothy 4:9
text: Do your best to come to me speedily,

title: II Timothy 4:10
text: for Demas has deserted me for love of this present world, and is gone to Thessalonica; Crescens is gone to Galatia; Titus to Dalmatia.

title: II Timothy 4:11
text: Luke only is with me. Pick up Mark, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me in my ministry.

title: II Timothy 4:12
text: Tychicus I have sent to Ephesus.

title: II Timothy 4:13
text: When you come, bring the cloak I left in Troas with Carpus; also my books, but especially my parchments.

title: II Timothy 4:14
text: Alexander, the coppersmith, manifested bitter hostility toward me. The Lord will requite him according to his works.

title: II Timothy 4:15
text: Be also on your guard against him, for he has violently opposed my arguments.

title: II Timothy 4:16
text: At the time of my first defense no one stood by me; on the contrary they all deserted me--may it not be laid to their charge!

title: II Timothy 4:17
text: Nevertheless the Lord Jesus stood by me, and strengthened my heart, that through me full proclamation of the gospel might be made, and the Gentiles might hear it; and I was rescued from the lion's jaws.

title: II Timothy 4:18
text: And the Lord will rescue me from every evil assault, and will preserve me for his heavenly kingdom. To him be the glory forever and ever! Amen!

title: II Timothy 4:19
text: Give my greetings to Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.

title: II Timothy 4:20
text: Erastus remained at Corinth; Trophimus I left behind me ill at Miletus.

title: II Timothy 4:21
text: Do try to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, and so do Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brotherhood.

title: II Timothy 4:22
text: The Lord Jesus be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.

title: Titus 1:1
text: To Titus, my true son in a common faith, from Paul, a slave of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, and to the knowledge of the truth which goes with piety;

title: Titus 1:2
text: I write in hope of life eternal which God who never lies, promised before times eternal,

title: Titus 1:3
text: but manifested in his own time; that word of his in proclaiming which I have been entrusted by command of God our Saviour.

title: Titus 1:4
text: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Saviour.

title: Titus 1:5
text: I left you in Crete for this reason, that you might set right the things left unfinished, and appoint presbyters in every city as I had instructed you;

title: Titus 1:6
text: men who are blameless, the husband of one wife, with believing children who are not accused of riot or insubordination.

title: Titus 1:7
text: For indeed a presiding officer, as God's steward, ought to be blameless, not self-willed or quick-tempered, not a drunkard or violent, or greedy of filthy lucre;

title: Titus 1:8
text: but he must be hospitable, a lover of the good, sober-minded, just, holy, self-controlled.

title: Titus 1:9
text: He must hold to the faithful word according to the teaching, so that he may be able both to encourage by sound teaching, and to confute our opponents.

title: Titus 1:10
text: For there are many individuals who are unruly, empty talkers and deceivers, particularly those of the circumcision, whose mouths must be stopped;

title: Titus 1:11
text: for they upset whole households and, for filthy lucre's sake, teach what they ought not to teach.

title: Titus 1:12
text: By one of their own number, by a prophet of their own, it has been said, "Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, idle gluttons."

title: Titus 1:13
text: This testimony is true. So rebuke them sharply,

title: Titus 1:14
text: so as to make them sound in the faith, not giving heed to Jewish myths and commandments of men who turn away from the truth.

title: Titus 1:15
text: All things are pure to the pure; but to the contaminated and the faithless nothing is pure, nay, their very minds and consciences are tainted.

title: Titus 1:16
text: They profess to know God, but by their deeds they disown him; in that they are detestable, disobedient, and reprobate for good work of any sort.

title: Titus 2:1
text: But do you, on your part, speak what becomes sound teaching;

title: Titus 2:2
text: that the older men be self-controlled, serious and sober-minded, sound in faith, in love, in patience;

title: Titus 2:3
text: that older women likewise be reverent in demeanor, not slanderers or slaves to much wine, but teachers of what is right.

title: Titus 2:4
text: They should train the younger women to love their husbands and children,

title: Titus 2:5
text: to be sober-minded, chaste, workers at home, kind and submissive to their husbands, in order that God's message be not maligned.

title: Titus 2:6
text: The younger men exhort to be sober-minded; in every respect showing yourself an example of good works.

title: Titus 2:7
text: In your teaching be serious and sincere.

title: Titus 2:8
text: Let the instruction that you give be sound and above reproach, so that our opponents may be ashamed because they find no evil things to say about us.

title: Titus 2:9
text: Exhort slaves to be obedient to their own masters, and to be well-pleasing to them in every respect;

title: Titus 2:10
text: not to contradict nor pilfer, but to exhibit praiseworthy trustworthiness in every thing, that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.

title: Titus 2:11
text: "For God's grace has shined forth bringing salvation to all men

title: Titus 2:12
text: And schooling us to renounce impiety and evil passions, And to live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present age;

title: Titus 2:13
text: While we look for the blessed hope and epiphany of the glory of our great God and Saviour, Jesus Christ.

title: Titus 2:14
text: He gave himself for us to redeem us from all iniquity, and to purify unto himself a people zealous of good works."

title: Titus 2:15
text: Thus speak, exhort, reprove with all authority. Let no one despise you.

title: Titus 3:1
text: Remind them to be submissive to their rulers and authorities; let them be obedient, ready for every good work;

title: Titus 3:2
text: they must speak evil of none, they must not be quarrelsome, but gentle, showing perfect meekness toward all.

title: Titus 3:3
text: For we were ourselves once foolish, disobedient, deceived, slaving for various lusts and pleasures, passing our lives in malice and envy. We were hateful, and we hated one another.

title: Titus 3:4
text: But when the kindness of God our Saviour, And his love toward men shined forth,

title: Titus 3:5
text: He saved us, not because of any deeds that we had done in righteousness, But because of his own pity for us. He saved us by that washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Spirit

title: Titus 3:6
text: which he poured out upon us richly, through Jesus Christ our Saviour;

title: Titus 3:7
text: In order that being justified by his grace, We might be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

title: Titus 3:8
text: This saying is trustworthy. On this I want you to firmly insist; that those who have faith in God must be careful to maintain honest occupations. Such counsels are good and profitable for men.

title: Titus 3:9
text: But avoid foolish questionings and genealogies and dissensions and wranglings about the law; for these are unprofitable and empty.

title: Titus 3:10
text: After a first and second admonition, refuse a man who is causing divisions;

title: Titus 3:11
text: you may be sure that such a man is perverted and sinning, and is self-condemned.

title: Titus 3:12
text: As soon as I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, join me in Nicopolis as quickly as you can, for I have arranged to winter there.

title: Titus 3:13
text: Speed Zenas the lawyer, and Apollos, on their journey diligently.

title: Titus 3:14
text: Let them want nothing, and "let our people learn to devote themselves to honest work to supply the necessities of their teachers," so that they be not unfruitful.

title: Titus 3:15
text: All who are with us salute you. Salute those who love me in faith. Grace be with you all.

title: Philemon 1:1
text: To my beloved friend and coworker Philemon,

title: Philemon 1:2
text: to my sister Apphia, to my fellow soldier Archippus, and to the church which meets at Philemon's house: From Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and brother Timothy:

title: Philemon 1:3
text: Grace and peace be to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

title: Philemon 1:4
text: I am ever mentioning you in my prayers, and giving thanks to God,

title: Philemon 1:5
text: because I am hearing of your love and of the faith which you hold, not only toward the Lord Jesus Christ, but toward all the saints.

title: Philemon 1:6
text: And I pray that your participation may become effectual, as you come to acknowledge every good thing which is in you to Christ.

title: Philemon 1:7
text: For I have great joy and comfort in your love, my brother, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed.

title: Philemon 1:8
text: And so, although I might be bold in Christ to dictate to you what is fitting,

title: Philemon 1:9
text: yet for love's sake, I rather beseech you, I, Paul, an old man, and now a prisoner for Christ Jesus!

title: Philemon 1:10
text: I beseech you for my son, Onesimus, whom I have begotten in these chains.

title: Philemon 1:11
text: Once you found him "unprofitable," but now he is "profitable" to you and to me.

title: Philemon 1:12
text: I am sending him back to you, he himself, that is, my very heart!

title: Philemon 1:13
text: I could wish to retain him at my side, so that he might minister to me in your stead, in my bonds for the gospel.

title: Philemon 1:14
text: But without your consent I was unwilling to do anything, so that your kindness to me might be of your own free will, and not of compulsion.

title: Philemon 1:15
text: Perhaps for this reason you were separated from him for an hour, in order that you might have him back forever,

title: Philemon 1:16
text: no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, as a brother beloved; especially dear to me, but how much more to you, both as a man and a fellow Christian.

title: Philemon 1:17
text: If then you count me as a partner, receive him as you would me.

title: Philemon 1:18
text: And if he has wronged you at all, or is owing you anything, charge that to me.

title: Philemon 1:19
text: I Paul am writing this in my own handwriting, "I will repay you." But I will not mention that you owe me, over and over, your very soul.

title: Philemon 1:20
text: Come my brother, let me have joy in the Lord because of you! Refresh my heart in Christ!

title: Philemon 1:21
text: Because I am thoroughly persuaded of your obedience, I have written you, knowing full well that you will do by me what I am asking.

title: Philemon 1:22
text: Please also prepare for me a lodging, for I am hoping by your prayers to be restored to you again.

title: Philemon 1:23
text: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greeting;

title: Philemon 1:24
text: so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.

title: Philemon 1:25
text: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

title: Hebrews 1:1
text: God, who in ancient days spoke to our ancestors in the prophets, at many different times and by various methods,

title: Hebrews 1:2
text: has at the end of these days spoken to us in a Son whom he appointed heir of all things; through whom also he made the universe.

title: Hebrews 1:3
text: He being an emanation of God's glory and stamp of his substance, and upholding the universe by the utterances of his power, after by himself making purification of our sins, has taken his seat on the right hand of the Majesty on High.

title: Hebrews 1:4
text: He is as much superior to the angels as the name that he has inherited surpasses theirs.

title: Hebrews 1:5
text: For to what angel did God ever say, Thou art my son; this day have I become thy Father? and again, I will be a father to him, and he shall be to me a son?

title: Hebrews 1:6
text: And further, when he brought the firstborn into the habitable world, he said, Let all the angels of God worship him.

title: Hebrews 1:7
text: While of the angels he said, He makes his angels into winds, His ministering servants into flames of fire.

title: Hebrews 1:8
text: But to the Son he says: Thy throne, O God, is forever and ever, And the scepter of thy kingdom is the scepter of justice.

title: Hebrews 1:9
text: Thou hast loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; Therefore did God, thy God, anoint thee with the oil of gladness beyond thy comrades.

title: Hebrews 1:10
text: And, Thou, O Lord, in the beginning didst lay the foundations of the earth, And the heavens are the work of thy hands.

title: Hebrews 1:11
text: They will perish, but thou remainest; They all will grow old like a garment,

title: Hebrews 1:12
text: Like a mantle thou wilt fold them up, And like a garment they will be changed. But thou art the same, And thy years will never fail.

title: Hebrews 1:13
text: To which of the angels has he ever said, Sit at my right hand, Till I make thy foes a footstool for thy feet?

title: Hebrews 1:14
text: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth for service in behalf of those who are about to inherit salvation?

title: Hebrews 2:1
text: For this reason we must pay the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, for fear we should drift away.

title: Hebrews 2:2
text: For if the word uttered through angels stood firm, so that every transgression and act of disobedience met with its just retribution, how shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation?

title: Hebrews 2:3
text: Which having begun to be spoken by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard him;

title: Hebrews 2:4
text: God himself corroborating their testimony by signs and wonders and a variety of miraculous powers, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit imparted in accordance with his own will.

title: Hebrews 2:5
text: It is not to angels that God subjected the age to be, of which we are speaking.

title: Hebrews 2:6
text: But some one, somewhere, testified, saying: What is Man, that thou art mindful of him? Or any man, that thou carest for him?

title: Hebrews 2:7
text: Thou hast made him only a little lower that the angels; With glory and honor hast thou crowned him; And hast set him to govern the works of thy hands;

title: Hebrews 2:8
text: Thou hast put all things under his feet. For this putting all things under man means leaving nothing not subject to him. But we do not yet see all things subject to him.

title: Hebrews 2:9
text: What we do see is Jesus, who was made for a time a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor, because of the suffering of death, in order that through God's grace he might taste death for every man.

title: Hebrews 2:10
text: For it befitted him, for whom and through whom all things exist, in bringing many sons to glory, to make the Pioneer of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

title: Hebrews 2:11
text: For both he who sanctifies and those whom he is sanctifying are all from One; for which reason he is not ashamed to call them brothers, saying:

title: Hebrews 2:12
text: I will proclaim thy name to my brothers; In the midst of the Church I will hymn thy praises.

title: Hebrews 2:13
text: And again, I myself will put my trust in God. And again, Lo, I and the children God has given me.

title: Hebrews 2:14
text: Therefore, since the children are sharers in flesh and blood, he also similarly partook of the same, in order that through death he might render powerless him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;

title: Hebrews 2:15
text: And might deliver those who through fear of death had been subject to life-long bondage.

title: Hebrews 2:16
text: For assuredly it is not angels, nay, it is the offspring of Abraham, whom he is ever taking by the hand.

title: Hebrews 2:17
text: And so it was necessary that he should in all points be made like his brothers, so that he might become a compassionate and faithful high priest, in all that relates to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

title: Hebrews 2:18
text: For inasmuch as he himself has suffered, being tempted, he is also able instantly to succor those who are tempted, he is also able instantly to succor those who are tempted.

title: Hebrews 3:1
text: Therefore, holy brothers, comrades of a heavenly calling, fix your thoughts then upon Jesus, the Apostle and High Priest of our confession.

title: Hebrews 3:2
text: How faithful he was to the God who appointed him! For while Moses also was faithful in all God's house,

title: Hebrews 3:3
text: Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, inasmuch as he who has built a house has higher honor than the house itself.

title: Hebrews 3:4
text: For every house has its builder; but he who built the universe is God.

title: Hebrews 3:5
text: And Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant, bearing testimony to a witness about to be spoken;

title: Hebrews 3:6
text: but Christ as a Son in his own house; and we are that house, if we retain the cheerful courage and pride of our hope firm unto the end.

title: Hebrews 3:7
text: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: If you hear God's voice today,

title: Hebrews 3:8
text: Continue not to harden your hearts as in the Provocation, On the day of temptation in the wilderness,

title: Hebrews 3:9
text: When your forefathers tried my forbearance And saw my deeds for forty years.

title: Hebrews 3:10
text: For this reason I was sore displeased with that generation, And said, "They are always wandering in their hearts; They have never learned my ways";

title: Hebrews 3:11
text: So I swore in my wrath, "They shall never enter into my rest."

title: Hebrews 3:12
text: See to it, brothers, that there shall never be in any one of you an evil and unbelieving heart, manifesting itself in apostasy from the living God.

title: Hebrews 3:13
text: On the contrary, encourage each other daily, so long as there is a "Today," so that no one of you is hindered by the deceitfulness of sin.

title: Hebrews 3:14
text: For we are become comrades of the Christ, if we hold our first title deed firm until the very end.

title: Hebrews 3:15
text: In the words of Scripture, Today, if you hear his voice, Do not continue to harden your hearts as at the Provocation.

title: Hebrews 3:16
text: For who were they that heard and yet provoked him? Was it not all who came out of Egypt under the leadership of Moses?

title: Hebrews 3:17
text: And with whom was he grieved for forty years? Was it not with those who had sinned, and whose dead bodies fell in the wilderness?

title: Hebrews 3:18
text: And to whom did he swear that they should never enter into his rest, if not to those who had proved faithless? So you see that it was through unbelief that they were not able to enter in.

title: Hebrews 4:1
text: Let us be on our guard, then, though there is a promise still standing of being admitted to his rest, lest any one of you should be found to have come short of it.

title: Hebrews 4:2
text: For the Good News is come to us just as it did to them. But the message they heard was of no benefit to them, because they did not share the faith of those who gave heed to it.

title: Hebrews 4:3
text: We are actually entering into that rest, we who have believed, as God has said,- In my wrath I swore-- "They shall not enter into my Rest," although his works were finished since the foundation of the world.

title: Hebrews 4:4
text: For he has said, somewhere, regarding the seventh day, And God rested on the seventh day from all his work.

title: Hebrews 4:5
text: And again in this passage, They shall not enter into my rest.

title: Hebrews 4:6
text: Since, then, it remains that some should enter into it, and since those who formerly had the Good News preached to them did not enter in because of unbelief,

title: Hebrews 4:7
text: he again fixes a day, saying long afterward by David's lips, in words already quoted, Today if you hear his voice, Continue not to harden your hearts.

title: Hebrews 4:8
text: For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not have spoken afterward of another day.

title: Hebrews 4:9
text: So there remains a Sabbath Rest for the people of God.

title: Hebrews 4:10
text: For whoever has entered into his rest has rested from his works, just as God did from his.

title: Hebrews 4:11
text: Let us, then, be earnest to enter into that rest, so that no one may fall into the same example of disobedience.

title: Hebrews 4:12
text: For living is the Word of God, and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the severance of soul form spirit, of both joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the very thoughts and conceptions of the heart.

title: Hebrews 4:13
text: And there is not a creature hidden form him, but all things are naked and laid prostrate before the eyes of him with whom we have to do.

title: Hebrews 4:14
text: Inasmuch, then, as we have a great High Priest, Jesus, the Son of God, who has passed through the heavens, let us hold fast our confession of faith.

title: Hebrews 4:15
text: For we have not a High Priest who cannot sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who has been tempted in all points like as we are, yet without sin.

title: Hebrews 4:16
text: Let us, then, draw near with glad boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy, and find grace to help us in our times of need.

title: Hebrews 5:1
text: For every high priest chosen from time to time from among men is appointed on behalf of men, in matters relating to God, to offer both gifts and sacrifices on behalf of sins.

title: Hebrews 5:2
text: He is able to deal gently with the ignorant and erring, since he himself also is encompassed with moral weakness,

title: Hebrews 5:3
text: and because of this weakness he is bound to offer sin-offerings not only for the people, but also for himself.

title: Hebrews 5:4
text: Again no one takes this honorable office for himself, but he is called by God, just as Aaron was.

title: Hebrews 5:5
text: So even the Christ was not raised to the high glory of the priesthood by himself, but on the contrary by Him who said to him: Thou art my Son; this day have I become thy Father;

title: Hebrews 5:6
text: and again, Thou art a priest forever, after the order of Melchisedek.

title: Hebrews 5:7
text: In the days of his flesh, with better cries and weeping Jesus offered up prayers and supplications to Him who was able to save him out of death; and he was heard because of his devout submission.

title: Hebrews 5:8
text: Though he was a son, yet learned he obedience through the things which he suffered;

title: Hebrews 5:9
text: and by being thus made perfect, he became the source of enduring salvation to all who obey him,

title: Hebrews 5:10
text: while God himself pronounced him High Priest according to the order of Melchisedek.

title: Hebrews 5:11
text: Concerning him I have much to say, and much that is hard to make clear to you, because you have grown dull of hearing.

title: Hebrews 5:12
text: And this too, although you ought by this time to be teaching others, you are still needing some one to teach you the very rudiments of divine revelation. You need milk, not solid food.

title: Hebrews 5:13
text: For every one who feeds on milk is inexperienced in the word of righteousness. He is still an infant.

title: Hebrews 5:14
text: But solid food is for adults, that is, for those who by constant practise have their faculties trained to discriminate between good and evil.

title: Hebrews 6:1
text: So let us get beyond the teaching of the elementary doctrines of Christ, and let us be borne along toward what is mature. Let us not be continually laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works,

title: Hebrews 6:2
text: of faith in God, of the teaching regarding ablutions and the laying on of hands, of the resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

title: Hebrews 6:3
text: And this we will do, if God permit.

title: Hebrews 6:4
text: For in the case of those who have been once for all enlightened and have tasted of the heavenly gift,

title: Hebrews 6:5
text: and become partakers of the Holy Spirit, and tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the Future Age,

title: Hebrews 6:6
text: and then fallen away, it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance. For they repeatedly crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and expose him to an open shame.

title: Hebrews 6:7
text: For land that has drunk the showers that now and again fall upon it, and produced vegetation useful for those for whom it was tilled, receives a blessing from God;

title: Hebrews 6:8
text: but if it produces thorns and thistles, it is considered worthless, and is in danger of being cursed, and its end will be to be burned.

title: Hebrews 6:9
text: But though we thus speak, we are persuaded better things of you, beloved, and things that accompany salvation.

title: Hebrews 6:10
text: For God is not unjust; he will not forget your work and the love you showed for his cause, in sending help to your fellow Christians, as you are still doing.

title: Hebrews 6:11
text: but I am longing that each of you continue to show the same diligence to realize the fulness of your hope, even to the end.

title: Hebrews 6:12
text: Then do not become slack, but be imitators of those who through faith and patience are inheriting the promises.

title: Hebrews 6:13
text: For when God make the promise to Abraham, since he could swear by none greater, he swore by himself, saying:

title: Hebrews 6:14
text: Surely I will bless you, and bless you; I will increase you, and increase you.

title: Hebrews 6:15
text: And so by patiently waiting, Abraham obtained the promise.

title: Hebrews 6:16
text: [I am referring to the oath] because men swear by what is greater than themselves, and in every dispute of theirs the oath is final for confirmation.

title: Hebrews 6:17
text: On which principle God, wishing to show more convincingly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his purpose, mediated with an oath;

title: Hebrews 6:18
text: that by means of two immutable things--his promise and his oath-- in which it is impossible for God to break faith, we refugees may have strong encouragement to grasp the hope set before us.

title: Hebrews 6:19
text: This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, secure and strong, and passing into the sanctuary which is beyond the veil;

title: Hebrews 6:20
text: whither Jesus himself is entered as a forerunner on our behalf, having become a priest forever, after the order of Melchisedek.

title: Hebrews 7:1
text: It was this Melchisedek, King of Salem and Priest of the Most High God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him;

title: Hebrews 7:2
text: and it was to him that Abraham apportioned a tithe of all the spoil. He was first, as his name signifies, King of righteousness, and then King of Salem, that is, King of Peace;

title: Hebrews 7:3
text: without father or mother, without lineage, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest in perpetuity.

title: Hebrews 7:4
text: But observe how great this man was, to whom even Abraham, the Patriarch, gave a tenth part of the spoils.

title: Hebrews 7:5
text: Now those of the sons of Levi who are appointed to the priesthood, are authorized by the Law to take tithes of the people, that is, of their brothers, and that too, although these are descended from Abraham.

title: Hebrews 7:6
text: But this man who had no Levitical genealogy actually took tithes of Abraham, and blessed him to whom the promises belong.

title: Hebrews 7:7
text: Now it is beyond all controversy that the inferior is always blessed by the superior.

title: Hebrews 7:8
text: Again it is mortal men who receive tithes in the one case; while in the other it is he of whom it is attested, "He lives."

title: Hebrews 7:9
text: And even Levi, who is the receiver of tithes, so to speak, paid tithes through Abraham;

title: Hebrews 7:10
text: for Levi was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedek met Abraham.

title: Hebrews 7:11
text: Now if there were perfection through the Levitical priesthood, (and it was under it that the people received the Law) why was it still necessary for another kind of priest to arise, after the order of Melchisedek, instead of being reckoned according to the order of Aaron?

title: Hebrews 7:12
text: For when the priesthood changes, of necessity the law also changes.

title: Hebrews 7:13
text: He who is thus described belonged to another tribe, not one member of which has ever served at the altar.

title: Hebrews 7:14
text: For it is evident that our Lord was descended from Judah, a tribe of which Moses said nothing concerning the priesthood.

title: Hebrews 7:15
text: And this is yet more abundantly clear if, after the likeness of Melchisedek, there arises another Priest,

title: Hebrews 7:16
text: who has become such, not according to the law of a transitory enactment, but according to the energy of an indissoluble life.

title: Hebrews 7:17
text: For the words are in evidence, Thou art a priest forever after the order of Melchisedek.

title: Hebrews 7:18
text: For there is a setting aside of a foregoing commandment, because of its weakness and unprofitableness

title: Hebrews 7:19
text: (for the Law brought nothing to perfection); and there is the bringing in of a better hope by which we draw near to God;

title: Hebrews 7:20
text: mightier because it was not promised apart from an oath.

title: Hebrews 7:21
text: For although those priests became such without an oath, He had an oath form God who said to him, The Lord hath sworn and will not change, Thou art a priest forever.

title: Hebrews 7:22
text: And by so much Jesus becomes the guarantor of a better covenant.

title: Hebrews 7:23
text: And they indeed have been made priests, many in number, because they have been prevented by death from continuing;

title: Hebrews 7:24
text: but he, because of his abiding forever, holds his priesthood inviolable.

title: Hebrews 7:25
text: Hence also he is able to continue saving to the uttermost those who are ever drawing near to God through him, seeing that he is ever living to intercede for them.

title: Hebrews 7:26
text: For we needed just such a high priest, holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and exalted above the heavens;

title: Hebrews 7:27
text: one who has no need, like the high priests, to offer up daily sacrifices, first for his own sins, then for those of the people. For his sacrifice was made once for all, when he offered up himself.

title: Hebrews 7:28
text: For the Law appoints human beings to be high priests, men with all their weakness; but the word of the oath, which was later than the Law, appoints a Son, perfected forevermore.

title: Hebrews 8:1
text: The pith of all that we have been saying is this; we do have such a High Priest; and he has taken his seat on the right hand of the throne of Majesty in the heavens,

title: Hebrews 8:2
text: a minister of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, not man.

title: Hebrews 8:3
text: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices; whence it follows that this High Priest also must have some offering to make.

title: Hebrews 8:4
text: Now were he on earth, he would not even be a priest, since there are here those who present the gifts according to the Law--

title: Hebrews 8:5
text: those priests who serve a mere outline and shadow of the heavenly reality, just as Moses was divinely instructed when he was about to build the Tabernacle: "See", he says, "that you make everything on the pattern showed you on the mountain."

title: Hebrews 8:6
text: But Jesus has obtained a better ministry, by so much as he is also Mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted upon better promises.

title: Hebrews 8:7
text: For if the first covenant had been faultless, there would have been no need for a second.

title: Hebrews 8:8
text: But finding fault with them, He says: "There are days coming," says the Lord, "When I will establish with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah a new covenant;

title: Hebrews 8:9
text: Not according tot he covenant which I made with their forefathers, On the day when I took them by the hand to lead them forth out of the land of Egypt; For they did not continue in my covenant, And therefore I disregarded them," says the Lord.

title: Hebrews 8:10
text: "For this is the covenant which I will covenant with the house of Israel, After these days," says the Lord; "I will put my laws into their minds, And upon their hearts will I write them; And I will be their God, And they shall be my people;

title: Hebrews 8:11
text: And they shall not teach every man his fellow citizen, And every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord; For all shall know me, From the least to the greatest of them.

title: Hebrews 8:12
text: For I will have mercy upon their wrong-doings, And their sins I will remember no more."

title: Hebrews 8:13
text: By calling the covenant "new," He has made the first one obsolete; and whatever is becoming obsolete and aged, is near to vanishing.

title: Hebrews 9:1
text: Now even the first covenant had its ordinances of public worship, and its sanctuary, a material one.

title: Hebrews 9:2
text: For a tent was built, the outer one called the Holy Place, in which were the lamp and the table and the loaves of the Presence;

title: Hebrews 9:3
text: and behind the second veil was the tent called the Holy of Holies.

title: Hebrews 9:4
text: In it was the golden altar of incense, and also the Ark of the Covenant covered all over with gold, in which was a golden pot holding the manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;

title: Hebrews 9:5
text: while above it, overshadowing the mercy-seat, were the cherubim of glory. But I must not speak about these in detail.

title: Hebrews 9:6
text: Such then were the arrangements. Into the outer tent the priests enter continually in the performance of their duties;

title: Hebrews 9:7
text: but into the inner tent the high priest only goes alone, once a year, and that not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the ignorances of the people.

title: Hebrews 9:8
text: The Holy Spirit teaching by this that the way into the Holiest has not yet been disclosed while the first tent is still standing.

title: Hebrews 9:9
text: This is a parable, for the present time, according to which gifts and sacrifices are offered that are not able, as far as conscience is concerned, to perfect the worshiper;

title: Hebrews 9:10
text: since they consist only in meats and drinks and various ablutions, carnal ordinances, imposed until the time of reformation.

title: Hebrews 9:11
text: But when Christ came, a High Priest of good things to come, he passed through the greater and more perfect tent not made with hands, that is to say, not of this material creation,

title: Hebrews 9:12
text: not taking the blood of goats and oxen, but his own blood, and entered once for all into the Holy Place, obtaining for us an eternal redemption.

title: Hebrews 9:13
text: For if the blood of bulls and goats and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who have been defiled, sanctify to the cleansing of the flesh,

title: Hebrews 9:14
text: how much more shall the blood of Christ, who through his eternal spirit offered himself free from blemish to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works unto the service of an ever-living God!

title: Hebrews 9:15
text: And because of this he is the Mediator of a new testament, in order that, since a death has taken place to atone for offenses committed under the first testament, those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.

title: Hebrews 9:16
text: For where there is a testament, there must also be brought forward in evidence the death of the testator.

title: Hebrews 9:17
text: For a testament is only of force in case of the dead, being never valid so long as the testator lives.

title: Hebrews 9:18
text: Accordingly we find that not without blood was the first testament enacted.

title: Hebrews 9:19
text: For after every commandment according to the law had been spoken by Moses to the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people.

title: Hebrews 9:20
text: saying, This is the blood of that testament which God commanded in regard to you.

title: Hebrews 9:21
text: Moreover the tabernacle and all the vessels of service he sprinkled likewise, and indeed, according to the Law,

title: Hebrews 9:22
text: almost everything is purified by blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no remission of sins.

title: Hebrews 9:23
text: While, then, it was necessary that the copies of the heavenly things should be cleansed by such sacrifices, the heavenly things themselves required nobler sacrifices than these.

title: Hebrews 9:24
text: For it was not into a Sanctuary made by hands, a mere type of the reality, that Christ entered, but he entered into heaven itself, now to appear in the very presence of God on our behalf.

title: Hebrews 9:25
text: Nor did he enter to offer himself repeatedly, as the high priest entered into the sanctuary, year after year, with blood that was not his own;

title: Hebrews 9:26
text: (for in that case he would have needed to suffer repeatedly, ever since the foundation of the world;) but now, once for all, at the end of the ages, he has appeared to abolish sin, but the offering of himself.

title: Hebrews 9:27
text: And since it is appointed to men once to die, and after that the judgment;

title: Hebrews 9:28
text: so also the Christ, after being once for all offered to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, without sin, to those who wait for him for salvation.

title: Hebrews 10:1
text: For the Law, being only a shadow of the good things to come, and not their very substance, its priests cannot with the same sacrifice which year after year they offer continually, make perfect those who draw near.

title: Hebrews 10:2
text: Otherwise would they not have ceased to be offered? Because the worshippers having been once cleansed, would have had no more consciousness of sin.

title: Hebrews 10:3
text: But on the other hand, in these sacrifices sins are called to memory, year after year.

title: Hebrews 10:4
text: For it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sin.

title: Hebrews 10:5
text: It is for this reason that the Christ, on coming into the world, declared: Sacrifice and offerings thou dost not desire, But a body didst thou prepare for me;

title: Hebrews 10:6
text: In whole burnt offerings and sin offerings Thou hast taken no pleasure.

title: Hebrews 10:7
text: Then I said, "I am come--in the roll of the book it is written of me-- To do thy will, O God."

title: Hebrews 10:8
text: First when it is said, Thou hast no longing for, thou takest no delight in Sacrifices and offerings, or whole burnt offerings and sin offerings,

title: Hebrews 10:9
text: (offerings regularly made under the law), and then it is added, Lo, I come to do thy will, he does away with the first, in order that he may establish the second.

title: Hebrews 10:10
text: And it is by this will that we have been sanctified by the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

title: Hebrews 10:11
text: For while every priest stands, day after day, at his ministrations, and many times repeats the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins,

title: Hebrews 10:12
text: this Priest, after offering one Sacrifice for sins, sat down forever on God's right hand;

title: Hebrews 10:13
text: henceforth waiting until his enemies be put as the footstool of his feet.

title: Hebrews 10:14
text: For by one single offering he has perfected forever those whom he is sanctifying.

title: Hebrews 10:15
text: And the Holy Spirit also gives his testimony, when he said:

title: Hebrews 10:16
text: "This is the covenant I will make with them After those days," says the Lord: "I will set my laws upon their hearts, And I will inscribe them on their minds."

title: Hebrews 10:17
text: Then he adds, And their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.

title: Hebrews 10:18
text: But when these have been remitted, there is no more any offering for sin.

title: Hebrews 10:19
text: Since, then, we have a cheerful confidence, brothers, to enter into the Holiest by the blood of Jesus,

title: Hebrews 10:20
text: by the way which he dedicated for us, that new and living way, through the veil (that is, his flesh);

title: Hebrews 10:21
text: and since we have a great High Priest over the house of God;

title: Hebrews 10:22
text: let us draw near with a true heart, in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled from and evil conscience, and our bodies bathed in pure water.

title: Hebrews 10:23
text: Let us hold fast the confession of our hope, unwavering (for He is faithful who promised);

title: Hebrews 10:24
text: and let us consider one another, to provoke unto love and good works;

title: Hebrews 10:25
text: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the custom of some, but exhorting one another; all the more as you behold the Day drawing near.

title: Hebrews 10:26
text: For if we sin wilfully, after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains any other sacrifice for sins,

title: Hebrews 10:27
text: but a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and a fiery indignation which is about to devour the adversaries.

title: Hebrews 10:28
text: Any one who set at naught the law of Moses was put to death without pity, on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

title: Hebrews 10:29
text: How much surer, think you, will be the punishment of one who has trodden under foot the Son of God, and has profaned that covenant blood with which he was sanctified, and has done despite to the spirit of grace?

title: Hebrews 10:30
text: For we know Him who said, Vengeance is mine, I will repay, and again, The Lord will judge his people.

title: Hebrews 10:31
text: IT IS A FEARFUL THING TO FALL INTO THE HANDS OF THE LIVING GOD!

title: Hebrews 10:32
text: But ever call to mind the former days, in which, after having been enlightened, you endured a great conflict of sufferings;

title: Hebrews 10:33
text: partly by being made a public spectacle in reproaches and afflictions, and partly by sharing the fortunes of those that were so used.

title: Hebrews 10:34
text: For you did sympathize with the prisoners, and you did take joyfully the confiscation of your goods; conscious that you had for yourselves greater, even lasting possessions.

title: Hebrews 10:35
text: Now do not fling away your bold confidence, for it has a great recompense of reward.

title: Hebrews 10:36
text: For you need stedfastness, so that after having done the will of God, you may receive the promise,

title: Hebrews 10:37
text: For yet a very, very little while, and then The Coming One will have come, without delay.

title: Hebrews 10:38
text: But it is by faith that my Righteous One will live, And if he draws back, my soul takes no pleasure in him.

title: Hebrews 10:39
text: "But we are not of defections unto perdition, but of faith unto the gaining of the soul."

title: Hebrews 11:1
text: Now faith is the title-deed of things hoped for; the putting to the proof of things not seen.

title: Hebrews 11:2
text: For by it men of old times had witness borne to them.

title: Hebrews 11:3
text: By faith we understand that the world was fashioned by the Word of God, so that what we see was not made out of what is visible.

title: Hebrews 11:4
text: By faith Abel offered to God a sacrifice more acceptable than that of Cain, through which he had witness borne to him that he was righteous, God giving the testimony by accepting his gifts; and through it he, although he is dead, still speaks.

title: Hebrews 11:5
text: By faith Enoch was translated so that he should not see death; and he was not found, because God had translated him. Before his translation he had witness borne to him that he pleased God:

title: Hebrews 11:6
text: now without faith it is impossible to please him; for he who comes to God must believe that he is, and that he ever rewards those who are seeking.

title: Hebrews 11:7
text: By faith Noah, warned of God of things not yet seen, reverently gave heed, and built an ark for the saving of his house; by which he condemned the world, and became an heir of the righteousness which is of faith.

title: Hebrews 11:8
text: By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out unto a place which he was to receive for an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.

title: Hebrews 11:9
text: It was by faith that he sojourned in the promised land as an alien, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, his fellow heirs of the same promise.

title: Hebrews 11:10
text: For he continually looked for the city which has foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

title: Hebrews 11:11
text: By faith even Sarah herself received power to conceive seed, although she was past the age for child-bearing, because she counted Him faithful who had promised;

title: Hebrews 11:12
text: and thus there sprang from one man, and him practically dead, a nation like the stars in the heavens in multitude, or grains of sand upon the seashore, innumerable.

title: Hebrews 11:13
text: These all died in faith, not having yet received the promises; nay, but they saw them from afar, and hailed them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.

title: Hebrews 11:14
text: For those who say such things make it plain that they are seeking a Fatherland.

title: Hebrews 11:15
text: And if they had cherished the memory of that land from which they went out, they would have found an opportunity to return;

title: Hebrews 11:16
text: but now they are longing for a better homeland, that is, a heavenly. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God; and he has prepared a city for them.

title: Hebrews 11:17
text: By faith Abraham, when he was put to the test, was on the point of offering up Isaac; yes, he who had received the promise was about to offer up his only son,

title: Hebrews 11:18
text: of whom it had been said, It is through Isaac that your posterity will be traced.

title: Hebrews 11:19
text: For he accounted God able even to raise from the dead, from whence, figuratively speaking, he did indeed receive him back again.

title: Hebrews 11:20
text: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even concerning things to come.

title: Hebrews 11:21
text: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons, and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.

title: Hebrews 11:22
text: By faith Joseph, when his end was nigh, made mention of the exodus of the children of Israel, and gave instructions in regard to his bones.

title: Hebrews 11:23
text: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months by his parents, because they saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were not afraid of the king's decree.

title: Hebrews 11:24
text: By faith Moses, when he was grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,

title: Hebrews 11:25
text: choosing rather to share ill-treatment with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.

title: Hebrews 11:26
text: He accounted the obloquy of Christ to be greater than the treasures of Egypt; for he fixed his eyes on the reward.

title: Hebrews 11:27
text: By faith he left Egypt, not because he feared the wrath of the king, but he endured as seeing Him who is invisible.

title: Hebrews 11:28
text: By faith he established the Passover, and the sprinkling with blood, in order that the Destroying Angel might not touch the firstborn.

title: Hebrews 11:29
text: By faith the people crossed over the Red Sea as on dry land; and when the Egyptians tried to do this they were swallowed up.

title: Hebrews 11:30
text: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down after they had been encircled seven days.

title: Hebrews 11:31
text: By faith Rahab, the harlot, perished not with the disobedient, because she had received the spies in peace.

title: Hebrews 11:32
text: And what more shall I say? for time would fail me to tell of Gideon, of Barak, of Samson, and of Jeptha; of David and Samuel and the prophets,

title: Hebrews 11:33
text: who through faith conquered kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,

title: Hebrews 11:34
text: quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, proved valiant in warfare, and routed armies of aliens.

title: Hebrews 11:35
text: Woman received their dear ones alive from the dead; and others were broken on the wheel, not accepting the offered deliverance, in order that they might obtain a better resurrection.

title: Hebrews 11:36
text: Others again bore trial of mockings and scourgings, yes, even of chains and imprisonment.

title: Hebrews 11:37
text: They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, they were tempted, they were slain with the sword, they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins, being destitute, persecuted, tormented--

title: Hebrews 11:38
text: of whom the world was not worthy--wandering in deserts and mountains and caves and holes in the ground.

title: Hebrews 11:39
text: Yet, though these all had witness borne to them by their faith, they received not the promise;

title: Hebrews 11:40
text: since it was for us that God had in store some better thing, so that apart from us they should not be perfected.

title: Hebrews 12:1
text: Seeing then that we are encircled with this great cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and the sin that clings about us. Let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

title: Hebrews 12:2
text: looking unto Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured a cross, despising shame, and has now taken his seat at the right hand of the throne of God.

title: Hebrews 12:3
text: Compare yourselves with him who endured such hostility against himself at the hands of sinners, lest you grow weary, fainting in your souls.

title: Hebrews 12:4
text: Not yet have you resisted unto blood in your fight against sin;

title: Hebrews 12:5
text: and have you forgotten the exhortation which reasons with you as sons? My son, do not despise the training of the Lord, Nor faint when he corrects you;

title: Hebrews 12:6
text: For it is those whom he loves that he disciplines, And he scourges every son whom he acknowledges.

title: Hebrews 12:7
text: It is for discipline that you are enduring these sufferings. God is dealing with you as sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline?

title: Hebrews 12:8
text: If you are left without discipline, in which all children share, then are you bastards and not sons.

title: Hebrews 12:9
text: Furthermore, our earthly fathers used to discipline us, and we gave them reverence. Shall we not much rather be in subjection to the Father of spirits, and live?

title: Hebrews 12:10
text: For they only disciplined us for a few days, as seemed good to them; but he does it for our profit, that we may share his holiness.

title: Hebrews 12:11
text: Now no discipline seems for the present to be joyous, but grievous; but afterward it yields the peaceable fruits of righteousness to those who have been trained under it.

title: Hebrews 12:12
text: Wherefore lift up your listless hands, strengthen your feeble knees;

title: Hebrews 12:13
text: make straight path for your feet, so that what is lame may not be put out of joint, but rather be healed.

title: Hebrews 12:14
text: Run swiftly after peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.

title: Hebrews 12:15
text: Look carefully that there be no one who falls back from the grace of God; that no root of bitterness springs up to trouble you, and by its means many become defiled.

title: Hebrews 12:16
text: Take care lest there be any fornicator or scorner like Esau among you, who for one meal sold his birthright.

title: Hebrews 12:17
text: For you know that even when he afterward desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; he found no room for repentance, though he sought it earnestly, with tears.

title: Hebrews 12:18
text: For you are not come to a palpable and enkindled fire,

title: Hebrews 12:19
text: nor to gloom and darkness and tempest and the blare of a trumpet and an audible voice. Those who heard that voice entreated that no word more should be spoken to them.

title: Hebrews 12:20
text: For they could not endure that which was enjoined, Even if a wild beast touches the mountain it shall be stoned to death;

title: Hebrews 12:21
text: and so terrible was the scene that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and tremble.

title: Hebrews 12:22
text: On the contrary you are come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to innumerable hosts of angels,

title: Hebrews 12:23
text: to the festal assemblage and church of the firstborn, registered in heaven, to a Judge who is God of all, to the spirits of just men made perfect,

title: Hebrews 12:24
text: to Jesus the Mediator of the New Covenant, and to his sprinkled Blood whose message cries louder than that of Abel.

title: Hebrews 12:25
text: See that you do not refuse him who is speaking. For if they did not escape punishment when they refused to listen to their instructor on earth, much less shall we escape if we turn away from him who is teaching us from heaven;

title: Hebrews 12:26
text: whose voice then shook the earth, but now he has promised, saying, Once again, once for all, I make not only earth, but heaven also to tremble.

title: Hebrews 12:27
text: That phrase, "Once again," signifies the removal of the things which can be shaken, created things, in order that the things which cannot be shaken may remain.

title: Hebrews 12:28
text: Wherefore since we are receiving a kingdom which is unshakable, let us give thanks, and so offer acceptable worship to God, with holy awe and fear,

title: Hebrews 12:29
text: FOR INDEED OUR GOD IS A CONSUMING FIRE.

title: Hebrews 13:1
text: Let brotherly love continue.

title: Hebrews 13:2
text: Do not neglect to show hospitality; for by it some have even entertained angels unawares.

title: Hebrews 13:3
text: Remember those who are in prison, as if you were fellow prisoners; remember too, those who are being ill-treated, since you too, are in the body.

title: Hebrews 13:4
text: Let marriage be held in honor by all, and the marriage bed be undefiled; for fornicators and adulterers will God judge.

title: Hebrews 13:5
text: Let your life be untainted by love of money; be content with such things as you have; for God himself has said, I will never leave thee; I will never forsake thee.

title: Hebrews 13:6
text: So that we can say with confidence, The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?

title: Hebrews 13:7
text: Remember your leaders, the men who spoke the message of God to you; consider the issue of their lives, and imitate their faith.

title: Hebrews 13:8
text: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: Hebrews 13:9
text: Do not allow yourselves to be swept away by various and strange teachings. For it is a beautiful thing to be established in heart by grace, and not by regulations regarding food, from which those that occupied themselves with them have derived no benefit.

title: Hebrews 13:10
text: We Christians have an altar from which those have no right to eat who minister in the Tabernacle.

title: Hebrews 13:11
text: For the bodies of the animals whose blood is carried by the High Priest into the Holy Place are burned outside the camp,

title: Hebrews 13:12
text: and so Jesus suffered outside the gate in order to sanctify the people by his own blood.

title: Hebrews 13:13
text: Let us then go forth to him outside the camp, bearing his reproach.

title: Hebrews 13:14
text: For we have not here an abiding city, but we are earnestly seeking the city that is to be.

title: Hebrews 13:15
text: In his name, then, let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is the fruit of lips that confess his name.

title: Hebrews 13:16
text: And forget not to be kind and liberal; for with that sort of sacrifice God is well pleased.

title: Hebrews 13:17
text: Obey your leaders and submit to them; for they are keeping watch over your souls, as those who must give account; that they may do thus with joy and not with lamentation, for this would be unprofitable to you.

title: Hebrews 13:18
text: Keep on praying for me. I am persuaded that I have a clear conscience, and I desire in every way to live nobly.

title: Hebrews 13:19
text: I the more earnestly ask for your prayers, that I may be the more speedily restored to you.

title: Hebrews 13:20
text: Now the God of peace, who brought up from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of an eternal covenant,

title: Hebrews 13:21
text: equip you in every good deed for the doing of his will, doing in you what is well-pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ. To him be the glory unto the ages of the ages! Amen!

title: Hebrews 13:22
text: But I entreat you, brothers, bear with my word of exhortation, for I have written to you briefly.

title: Hebrews 13:23
text: You know that our brother Timothy has been set free. If he comes soon, I will see him with you.

title: Hebrews 13:24
text: Salute all your leaders and the saints. The brothers from Italy send you greeting.

title: Hebrews 13:25
text: Grace be with you all, Amen.

title: James 1:1
text: James, a slave of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, sends greeting to the twelve tribes that are scattered abroad.

title: James 1:2
text: My brothers, when you are beset by various temptations, count it all joy,

title: James 1:3
text: because you know that the testing of your faith is working out endurance.

title: James 1:4
text: But let endurance have its perfect work, so that you may be perfect and entire, not lacking in anything.

title: James 1:5
text: If any one of you is lacking in wisdom, let him ask it from the God who gives to all men freely and without upbraiding; and it will be given to him.

title: James 1:6
text: But let him ask in faith, without wavering; for he who wavers is like a surge of the sea, wind-driven and tossed.

title: James 1:7
text: Such a man need not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord,

title: James 1:8
text: double-minded as he is, unstable at every turn.

title: James 1:9
text: Let a brother in humble circumstances glory in his exaltation;

title: James 1:10
text: but a rich brother, in his humiliation; because like the flower of the grass the rich man will pass away.

title: James 1:11
text: For as the sun comes up with a burning heat, it withers the grass, and its flowers fall, and the grace of the fashion of it perishes; so also shall the rich man fade away amid his pursuits.

title: James 1:12
text: Blessed is the man who endures temptation; for when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life which the Lord has promised to those who love him.

title: James 1:13
text: When he is being tempted, let no one say, "It is God who tempts me," for God cannot be tempted with evil, nor does he tempt any man.

title: James 1:14
text: But each man is tempted by his own lusts that allure and entice him.

title: James 1:15
text: Then lust conceives and gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is mature, brings forth death.

title: James 1:16
text: Do not be deceived, my brothers!

title: James 1:17
text: Every good gift and every perfect boon is from above, and is ever coming down to us from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom is no variation nor shadow of eclipse.

title: James 1:18
text: Because he willed, he gave us birth through the word of truth, so that we should be a kind of first-fruits among his creatures.

title: James 1:19
text: Mark this well, my dear brothers. Let every man be swift in hearing, slow in speaking, slow in growing angry;

title: James 1:20
text: for a man's anger does not further the righteous purpose of God.

title: James 1:21
text: So strip off all filthiness and superfluity of wickedness, and in meekness receive the implanted Word, which is able to save your souls.

title: James 1:22
text: And become doers of the Word, and not merely hearers, deceiving yourselves.

title: James 1:23
text: Because if any one is a hearer of the Word and not a doer, he is like a man who looks at his natural face in a mirror;

title: James 1:24
text: for after he has looked carefully at himself, he goes away, and at once forgets what he is like.

title: James 1:25
text: But the man who looks closely into the perfect law--the law of liberty--and continues looking, this man will be blessed in his deed because he is not a hearer who forgets, but a doer who does.

title: James 1:26
text: If a man thinks himself to be religious, and yet does not bridle his tongue, but deceives his own religion,

title: James 1:27
text: and undefiled before our God and Father, to look after orphans and widows in their affliction, and ever to keep himself unspotted from the world.

title: James 2:1
text: My brothers, do not hold the faith of the Lord Jesus, the Lord of Glory, in a spirit of caste.

title: James 2:2
text: Suppose a man comes into your synagogue with a gold ring and dazzling clothes, and suppose a poor man comes in, also, in shabby clothes,

title: James 2:3
text: and you look up to him who wears the fine clothing, and say to him, "Sit here in this fine place!" and to the poor man you say, "Stand there!" or "Sit on the floor at my feet!"

title: James 2:4
text: are you not drawing distinctions among yourselves, and have you not become judges with evil thoughts?

title: James 2:5
text: Listen, my dear brothers, has not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith, and to inherit the kingdom which he has promised to those who love him?

title: James 2:6
text: But you have dishonored the poor man. Do not the rich oppress you and drag you to court?

title: James 2:7
text: Are they not blaspheming that glorious Name by which you are called?

title: James 2:8
text: If you are keeping the royal law, which says, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thou dost thyself, you are doing well.

title: James 2:9
text: If you have the spirit of caste you are committing sin, and are convicted by the Law as transgressors.

title: James 2:10
text: For if a man keeps the whole of the Law, and yet stumbles in one point, he is guilty of all.

title: James 2:11
text: For he who said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not Kill. Now if you do not commit adultery, but if you do kill, you have transgressed the Law.

title: James 2:12
text: So speak and act like men who are to be judged by the law of liberty.

title: James 2:13
text: For judgment is without mercy to the man who has showed no mercy: but mercy glories in the face of judgment.

title: James 2:14
text: My brothers, what good is it if any one says that he has faith, if he has no deeds? Can such faith save him?

title: James 2:15
text: If a brother or sister be naked and in need of daily food,

title: James 2:16
text: and one of you says to them, "Depart in peace, find warmth and food for yourselves," but at the same time you do not give the necessaries of the body, what good would that do them?

title: James 2:17
text: In just the same way faith, if it have not deeds, is by itself a lifeless thing.

title: James 2:18
text: Some one indeed may say, "You have faith, and I have deeds." "Then show me your faith," I answer, "apart from any deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds."

title: James 2:19
text: You believe that God is one? You do well; even the demons believe, and they shudder.

title: James 2:20
text: But do you want to be convinced, O foolish man, that faith apart from deeds is barren?

title: James 2:21
text: Was not Abraham our ancestor justified by deeds, in that he offered up Isaac, his son, upon the altar?

title: James 2:22
text: You see how faith was cooperating with deeds, and faith was made perfect by deeds.

title: James 2:23
text: And the Scripture was fulfilled which said, And Abraham believed God, and this was imputed to him as righteousness, and he was called God's friend.

title: James 2:24
text: You see, then, that it is by his deeds a man is justified, and not simply by his faith.

title: James 2:25
text: In like manner was not Rahab, the harlot, justified by her deeds, in the fact that she received the messengers and sent them forth by another way?

title: James 2:26
text: So just as the body without a spirit is dead, so faith is dead without deeds.

title: James 3:1
text: Do not become many teachers, my brothers, because you know well that we teachers shall be judged by a severer standard than others.

title: James 3:2
text: For in many respects we often stumble. If any man never stumbles in speech, the same is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body as well.

title: James 3:3
text: When we put bits in the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we control their whole body also.

title: James 3:4
text: Look at the ships too, though they are so large, even when driven by fierce winds they are turned by a very small rudder, wherever the impulse of the helmsman wills.

title: James 3:5
text: So also the tongue is a small member and makes great boasts. Behold, how great a forest is set on fire by a little spark!
